title: Who are “the spirits in prison”, and when, where and what did he preach (1 Peter 3:19–20)?
summary: 1 Peter 3:19 says that “he went and preached unto the spirits in prison”, and 3:20 says they “sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah”. The verses do not say who “he” is in the act of going, what the prison is or where, when the going took place, or what the preaching was.
text: KJV 1 Peter 3:19: “By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 1 Peter 3:19: ἐν ᾧ καὶ τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνεύμασιν πορευθεὶς ἐκήρυξεν [in which also, having gone, he proclaimed to the spirits in prison]; the Textus Receptus text served prints the same words. KJV 1 Peter 3:20: “Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah”. KJV 1 Peter 3:18: “being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/60/3/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/60/3/.
reasoning: The verse gives an act (“went and preached”) and its hearers (“the spirits in prison”), and the next verse says of them that they were disobedient in the days of Noah. It does not say what “in which” (“By which”) points back to, whether the spirits are the persons who lived in Noah’s day, or other beings, when the going and preaching happened, or whether the preaching offered anything or announced something already done. The Greek printed is ἐκήρυξεν (proclaimed, preached) and the verse does not give the content. Readings that have been held include that the preaching was done by Christ through the Spirit in Noah’s day, that it was done between his death and his rising, and that the spirits are fallen angels and not human persons. The verses quoted state none of these and the record does not choose among them.

title: Which is “a sin unto death”, and what is meant by death (1 John 5:16–17)?
summary: 1 John 5:16 distinguishes “a sin which is not unto death” from “a sin unto death”, and says of the second “I do not say that he shall pray for it”. The verses do not say what the sin unto death is, whether the death is bodily or of another kind, or whether “I do not say” forbids prayer or only declines to command it.
text: KJV 1 John 5:16: “If any man see his brother sin a sin which is not unto death, he shall ask, and he shall give him life for them that sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death: I do not say that he shall pray for it”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 1 John 5:16: ἔστιν ἁμαρτία πρὸς θάνατον· οὐ περὶ ἐκείνης λέγω ἵνα ἐρωτήσῃ [there is a sin toward death; I do not say that he should ask concerning that one]; the Textus Receptus text served prints the same words. KJV 1 John 5:17: “All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/62/5/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/62/5/.
reasoning: The verses name two kinds of sin by their end (“unto death” and “not unto death”) and say that a man may ask and life be given for one kind. They do not name the sin unto death, say whether the death is the death of the body, of the person’s standing, or another death, or say whether the brother who sins is a believer. They do not say what “I do not say that he shall pray for it” rules out: it declines to say that he shall pray; it does not in terms forbid prayer. Readings that have been held include a particular act of apostasy, a persistent refusal of the faith, and a sin for which the Law prescribed death. The verses quoted state none of these and the record does not choose among them.

The record does not say which reading is right and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more. title: Which destruction layer could match Jericho’s fall?
summary: Radiocarbon measurements place the sampled Middle Bronze destruction before a proposed c.1400 BCE conquest. Associating that layer with Joshua therefore creates a dating conflict.
text: KJV Joshua 6:24: “And they burnt the city with fire, and all that was therein: only the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron, they put into the treasury of the house of the Lord.” Bruins and van der Plicht (1995), pp. 213, 218–219, report charred grain at 3306 ± 7 radiocarbon years BP, calibrated then to the late seventeenth or sixteenth century BCE; their results do not support c.1400 BCE for that layer.
scope: The flag is conditional on identifying Joshua’s destruction with the sampled Middle Bronze layer. The calibration ranges in this study are preliminary, not an exact year. This is not a claim that Jericho had no later occupation or that a burn layer identifies its attackers. Joshua supplies no BCE year.

title: Darius the Mede and the succession at Babylon
summary: Daniel’s apparent sequence puts Darius the Mede before Cyrus. Babylonian evidence records Cyrus’s takeover in 539 BCE; a separate preceding Median kingship does not fit that reconstruction.
text: KJV Daniel 5:31: “And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old.” KJV Daniel 6:28: “So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.” The Nabonidus Chronicle, column iii.15–20, describes Cyrus’s army entering Babylon and Cyrus’s subsequent entry. Frye discusses the resulting succession problem and alternative readings of Daniel 6:28.
scope: A separate Median king before Cyrus is the disputed reading. Identification with Cyrus or a subordinate official has been proposed; the chronicle alone cannot rule out every identification. Darius the Mede must not be silently equated with the later Darius I.

title: Theudas before or after Judas’s census revolt?
summary: Acts puts Theudas before Judas’s census revolt. Josephus places Theudas under Fadus in 44–46 CE, after that census. The dates conflict if the two accounts mean the same Theudas.
text: KJV Acts 5:36: “For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.” KJV Acts 5:37: “After this man rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.” Josephus, Antiquities 20.5.1 (§§97–99), places Theudas’s suppression under Fadus. Antiquities 18.1.1 associates Judas with the assessment following Archelaus’s removal. The NABRE Acts 5:36–37 note dates Fadus’s administration to 44–46 CE and identifies the sequence problem.
scope: This is a chronological conflict conditional on a shared identity. Acts does not give Theudas an absolute year; the earlier date is inferred from its sequence. Another earlier man of the same name is a proposed explanation, not an independently demonstrated identification.

title: “He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap” — the Greek has “as in a wineskin”
summary: The KJV has God gather the sea waters “as an heap”. The Septuagint, in Brenton’s Greek, has ὡσεὶ ἀσκόν, “as in a wineskin”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Psalm 33:7: “He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap: he layeth up the depth in storehouses.” Hebrew (WLC) Psalm 33:7: כֹּנֵ֣ס כַּ֭נֵּד מֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם נֹתֵ֖ן בְּאֹצָרֹ֣ות תְּהֹומֹֽות׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Psalm 32:7: Συνάγων ὡσεὶ ἀσκὸν ὕδατα θαλάσσης, τιθεὶς ἐν θησαυροῖς ἀβύσσους. [Gathering the waters of the sea as in a wineskin, putting abysses in storehouses.] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/33/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PSA032.htm.

New draft supplemental text (reported, unverified):
KJV Psalms 33:7: “He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap: he layeth up the depth in storehouses.” Hebrew (WLC) 33:7: כֹּנֵ֣ס כַּ֭נֵּד מֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם נֹתֵ֖ן בְּאֹצָרֹ֣ות תְּהֹומֹֽות׃. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 32:7: Συνάγων ὡσεὶ ἀσκὸν ὕδατα θαλάσσης, τιθεὶς ἐν θησαυροῖς ἀβύσσους. [Gathering the waters of the sea as a wineskin, putting the deeps in storehouses]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/33/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PSA032.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
A heap is a pile of water standing up, and a wineskin is a bag that holds it. The KJV has the former. The Greek has ὡσεὶ ἀσκὸν. The Hebrew has כַּ֭נֵּד in that slot, and the KJV reading follows it. The two English pictures differ: waters piled up against a limit, or waters held inside a container.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
A heap is a pile of the waters standing on one another. A skin bottle is a vessel that holds them. The Greek ἀσκός is the word for a leather bag or wineskin, and Brenton’s English prints “bottle”. The two texts give two pictures of how the sea is gathered, as a mound in the KJV and as the contents of a container in the Greek.

title: “Slay them not” (Psalm 59:11) — “Consume them in wrath, consume them, that they may not be” (59:13)
summary: In one prayer the speaker asks that his enemies not be slain, lest his people forget, and two verses later asks that they be consumed so that they are no more.
text: KJV Psalm 59:11: “Slay them not, lest my people forget: scatter them by thy power; and bring them down, O Lord our shield.” KJV Psalm 59:13: “Consume them in wrath, consume them, that they may not be: and let them know that God ruleth in Jacob unto the ends of the earth. Selah.” Hebrew (WLC) Psalm 59:12: אַל־תַּהַרְגֵ֤ם ׀ פֶּֽן־יִשְׁכְּח֬וּ עַמִּ֗י הֲנִיעֵ֣מֹו בְ֭חֵילְךָ וְהֹורִידֵ֑מֹו מָֽגִנֵּ֣נוּ אֲדֹנָֽי׃ Hebrew (WLC) Psalm 59:14: כַּלֵּ֥ה בְחֵמָה֮ כַּלֵּ֪ה וְֽאֵ֫ינֵ֥מֹו וְֽיֵדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־אֱ֭לֹהִים מֹשֵׁ֣ל בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב לְאַפְסֵ֖י הָאָ֣רֶץ סֶֽלָה׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Psalm 58:12: Μὴ ἀποκτείνῃς αὐτοὺς, μήποτε ἐπιλάθωνται τοῦ νόμου σου· διασκόρπισον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ δυνάμει σου, καὶ κατάγαγε αὐτοὺς ὁ ὑπερασπιστής μου Κύριε. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Psalm 58:14: συντέλειαι, ἐν ὀργῇ συντελείας, καὶ οὐ μὴ ὑπάρξουσι· καὶ γνώσονται ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ Ἰακὼβ δεσπόζει τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς· διάψαλμα. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/PSA059.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/59/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PSA058.htm.
reasoning: Verse 11 asks that the enemies not be killed, giving a reason (so that the people do not forget) and asking instead that they be scattered and brought down. Verse 13 asks that they be consumed in wrath until they are not. The Hebrew keeps the contrast: אַל־תַּהַרְגֵ֤ (do not kill them) and כַּלֵּ֥ה twice (finish, consume) with וְֽאֵ֫ינֵ֥מֹו (and they are not). The Greek has Μὴ ἀποκτείνῃς αὐτοὺς (do not kill them) and καὶ οὐ μὴ ὑπάρξουσι (and they shall not exist). The KJV and Hebrew juxtapose requests to spare and to consume. The Greek also juxtaposes not killing and destruction, but its destruction clause is not grammatically identical to the Hebrew imperatives. This does not establish inconsistent intentions.
scope: This sets two requests of one prayer beside each other in the KJV, the Hebrew and the Greek. It does not say the psalm contradicts itself or that the writer was inconsistent. The two verses may be read as two stages (scattering now, consuming later), or “not be” may mean their power or standing rather than their lives; the psalm does not say which. Both are the speaker’s prayers, not statements about what God does. The verses are poetry and the comparison is of the words printed. This record compares the requests in verses 11 and 13; it does not claim that the KJV, Hebrew and Greek agree in all details. Greek 58:12 has “your law” where Hebrew 59:12/KJV 59:11 has “my people”; the separate translation finding retains Brenton’s variant note. title: “Sore broken us in the place of dragons” — the Greek has “a place of affliction”
summary: In the KJV the speakers say God has sore broken them “in the place of dragons”. The Septuagint, in Brenton’s Greek, has ἐν τόπῳ κακώσεως, “in a place of affliction”, where the KJV has “dragons”.
text: KJV Psalm 44:19: “Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.” Hebrew (WLC) Psalm 44:20: כִּ֣י דִ֭כִּיתָנוּ בִּמְקֹ֣ום תַּנִּ֑ים וַתְּכַ֖ס עָלֵ֣ינוּ בְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Psalm 43:20: Ὅτι ἐταπείνωσας ἡμᾶς ἐν τόπῳ κακώσεως, καὶ ἐπεκάλυψεν ἡμᾶς σκιὰ θανάτου. [Because you humbled us in a place of affliction, and the shadow of death covered us.] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/44/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PSA043.htm.
reasoning: Both texts name the place where the people were crushed or brought low. The KJV names it “the place of dragons”, a place where creatures live. The Greek names it τόπῳ κακώσεως, a place of affliction or ill-treatment, which names a condition and not a creature. The Hebrew has תַּנִּ֑ים in the same slot, and the KJV reading follows it. A reader of the English pictures a lair of creatures; a reader of the Greek pictures a place of suffering.
scope: T applies at 44:19 and only to the noun; the rest of the verse (the shadow of death covering them) agrees. The difference found is between the KJV and the Greek. The Hebrew is quoted so that the three texts stand together; this record does not say what the Hebrew word means, and does not say that “dragons” is wrong. The Greek verb of the first half (ἐταπείνωσας, “you humbled”) also differs from the KJV “sore broken”; it is not tagged separately. A published record on Job 30:29 notes a comparable Greek reading for a similar Hebrew noun. This compares the wording of three texts and does not show which is original. title: “That seek thy face, O Jacob” — the Greek has “the face of the God of Jacob”
summary: In the KJV the seekers are addressed as “Jacob”, and the face they seek is “thy face”. The Septuagint, in Brenton’s Greek, has them seek τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ Θεοῦ Ἰακώβ, “the face of the God of Jacob”.
text: KJV Psalm 24:6: “This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek thy face, O Jacob. Selah.” Hebrew (WLC) Psalm 24:6: זֶ֭ה דֹּ֣ור [דֹּרְשֹׁו כ] (דֹּרְשָׁ֑יו ק) מְבַקְשֵׁ֨י פָנֶ֖יךָ יַעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Psalm 23:6: Αὕτη ἡ γενεὰ ζητούντων αὐτὸν, ζητούντων τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ Θεοῦ Ἰακώβ. διάψαλμα. [This is the generation of those who seek him, who seek the face of the God of Jacob.] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/24/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PSA023.htm.
reasoning: In the KJV the verse turns to speak to a person or a people named Jacob (“O Jacob”), and the face sought is the face of the one addressed earlier. reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The Hebrew has הַלְּבָנָה, “the white one”, the usual poetic word for the moon, and הַחַמָּה, “the hot one”, the sun. The Greek has the nouns for brick (πλίνθος) and wall (τεῖχος). In unpointed Hebrew the word for the moon (לבנה) has the same consonants as the word for a brick (לְבֵנָה), and the word for the sun (חמה) is close to the word for a wall (חומה). The KJV reads the heavenly bodies and the Greek reads building materials. The result is two different pictures at the moment of the Lord’s reign.

The Hebrew has לַגַּד and לַמְנִי (gad and meni). The KJV renders them as the common nouns “troop” and “number”. The Greek gives two powers to whom the table and the cup are offered: a δαιμόνιον and Τύχη, Fortune. A reader of the English meets a crowd and a count; a reader of the Greek meets two objects of worship.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew has הַעֹרְכִים לַגַּד שֻׁלְחָן וְהַמְמַלְאִים לַמְנִי מִמְסָךְ, “those setting for Gad a table, and those filling for Meni a mixed [drink]”. The prefixed ל is a preposition; it does not by itself prove that the words are proper names. NET’s translator notes identify Gad and Meni as deity names and cite HALOT. The KJV renders them as “that troop” and “that number”, as common nouns, and not as names. The Greek has τῷ δαιμονίῳ, “to the demon”, and τῇ τύχῃ, “to fortune”, and treats the objects of the offering as divine or spiritual beings.
scope: T applies at Isaiah 65:11, Septuagint only. The Hebrew לַגַּד and לַמְנִי are quoted as background. NET’s translator notes identify them as deity names; that has not been checked against a primary lexicon, so no Hebrew finding is made.

title: “He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man” — the Greek has “the transgressor that sacrifices a calf is as he that kills a dog”
summary: The KJV compares a worshipper’s sacrifice with a crime: “He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog’s neck.” Brenton’s Greek has Ὁ δὲ ἄνομος ὁ θύων μοι μόσχον, ὡς ὁ ἀποκτέννων κύνα — “The lawless one who sacrifices a calf to me is as one who kills a dog” — with a single transgressor and one pair of acts.
text:

Yea, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations.” Hebrew (WLC) Isaiah 66:3: שֹׁוחֵ֨ט הַשֹּׁ֜ור מַכֵּה־אִ֗ישׁ זֹובֵ֤חַ הַשֶּׂה֙ עֹ֣רֵֽף כֶּ֔לֶב מַעֲלֵ֤ה מִנְחָה֙ דַּם־חֲזִ֔יר מַזְכִּ֥יר לְבֹנָ֖ה מְבָ֣רֵֽךְ אָ֑וֶן גַּם־הֵ֗מָּה בָּֽחֲרוּ֙ בְּדַרְכֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְשִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֖ם נַפְשָׁ֥ם חָפֵֽצָה׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Isaiah 66:3: Ὁ δὲ ἄνομος ὁ θύων μοι μόσχον, ὡς ὁ ἀποκτέννων κύνα· ὁ δὲ ἀναφέρων σεμίδαλιν, ὡς αἷμα ὕειον· ὁ διδοὺς λίβανον εἰς μνημόσυνον, ὡς βλάσφημος. Καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐξελέξαντο τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰ βδελύγματα αὐτῶν ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτῶν ἠθέλησε. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/23/66/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ISA66.htm.

reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The KJV has four pairs of offering and offence (ox and man, lamb and dog’s neck, oblation and swine’s blood, incense and blessing an idol). The Greek has three (calf and dog, fine flour and swine’s blood, frankincense and blasphemy). It names the sacrificer ἄνομος, “lawless”, which the KJV does not. The offerings are also not the same: ox against calf, and the lamb pair is not in the Greek.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew has שׁוֹחֵט הַשּׁוֹר מַכֵּה־אִישׁ, “one slaughtering the ox, one striking a man”, then זוֹבֵחַ הַשֶּׂה עֹרֵף כֶּלֶב, “one sacrificing the lamb, one breaking a dog’s neck”. The Greek has a single clause for the offering of a calf: ὁ θύων μοι μόσχον, ὡς ὁ ἀποκτέννων κύνα, “the one sacrificing a calf to me, as one killing a dog”. The man-slaying comparison is not there, and the offerer is called ἄνομος, “lawless”. The last comparison also differs: the KJV has “as if he blessed an idol” (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן); the Greek has ὡς βλάσφημος, “as a blasphemer”.

title: “Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow” — the Greek has “Phud, and Lud, and Mosoch”
summary: In the KJV the escaped are sent “to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal, and Javan”. Brenton’s Greek has εἰς Θαρσίς, καὶ Φούδ, καὶ Λούδ, καὶ Μοσόχ, καὶ εἰς Θοβέλ, καὶ εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα — “to Tarsis, and Phud, and Lud, and Mosoch, and to Thobel, and to Greece”.
text:

Preserved draft reasoning:
The Hebrew has פּוּל וְלוּד מֹשְׁכֵי קֶשֶׁת, which the KJV reads as Pul and Lud, “that draw the bow” (a description). The Greek reads the participle as a place or people name, Mosoch (Meshech), so that the list has an extra nation in place of the description. The Greek also has Phud where the KJV has Pul, and Greece (Ἑλλάς) where the KJV has Javan.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew has וְלוּד מֹשְׁכֵי קֶשֶׁת, “and Lud, drawers of the bow”, where מֹשְׁכֵי is a plural participle, “those drawing”. The Greek has καὶ Λοὺδ, καὶ Μοσόχ, “and Lud, and Mosoch”, and no word for bow. The KJV has a description of the people of Lud; the Greek has a separate place or people. Mosoch has the same consonants as the Hebrew name Meshech (מֶשֶׁךְ), which is not in this verse. Under the owner’s ruling on ordinary-word names this is the reverse case: the Greek has a name where the Hebrew has ordinary words.

title: “The golden city ceased” — the Greek has “the taskmaster has ceased”
summary: In the KJV the proverb against the king of Babylon says “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Brenton’s Greek reads “How has the exactor (ὁ ἀπαιτῶν) ceased, and the taskmaster (ὁ ἐπισπουδαστής) ceased?” where the KJV has “the golden city”.
text: KJV Isaiah 14:4: “That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Hebrew (WLC) Isaiah 14:4: וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה עַל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאָמָ֑רְתָּ אֵ֚יךְ שָׁבַ֣ת נֹגֵ֔שׂ שָׁבְתָ֖ה מַדְהֵבָֽה׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Isaiah 14:4: Καὶ λήψῃ τὸν θρῆνον τοῦτον ἐπὶ τὸν βασιλέα Βαβυλῶνος, Πῶς ἀναπέπαυται ὁ ἀπαιτῶν, καὶ ἀναπέπαυται ὁ ἐπισπουδαστής; Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/23/14/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ISA14.htm.
reasoning: The first half of the line agrees: a person who exacts or oppresses has ceased. The second half differs in kind. The KJV has a place, “the golden city”. The Greek has a second person who drives or presses others, a title parallel to the first. The Hebrew word is מַדְהֵבָה, which occurs only here; the KJV takes it as a golden place and the Greek as a person.
scope: T applies at 14:4, second clause, only. The difference found is between the KJV and the Greek. The Hebrew is quoted so that the three texts stand together; this record does not say what מַדְהֵבָה means. The Hebrew is a word that occurs once, so it cannot be checked against other uses in the same book. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees, and this record compares the wording of the texts and does not show which reading is original.

title: “He is gone up to Bajith, and to Dibon” — Brenton’s Greek has “Debon, where your altar is”
summary: KJV Isaiah 15:2 has Moab going up to “Bajith, and to Dibon, the high places”. The Hebrew edition quoted prints הַבַּיִת וְדִיבֹן. Brenton’s Greek prints Δηβών, οὗ ὁ βωμὸς ὑμῶν, “Debon, where your altar is”, and prints no word that corresponds to Bajith.

Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/23/15/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ISA15.htm.
reasoning: At 15:2 the Hebrew הַבַּיִת is “the house” with the article; the KJV takes it as the place name Bajith and the Greek has no such place, and gives “where your altar is”, a place of worship.
scope: T applies at Isaiah 15:2, Septuagint only. The Hebrew is background; this record does not decide whether Bajith is a place or “the house”. This compares Brenton’s printed edition and does not establish which reading is original or that every manuscript agrees.

title: “Even all the chief ones of the earth” — the Greek calls them “all the giants who ruled the earth”
summary: In the KJV the dead who rise to meet the king of Babylon are all the chief ones of the earth. In Brenton’s Greek they are all the giants who ruled the earth.
text: KJV Isaiah 14:9: “Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.” Hebrew (WLC) 14:9: שְׁאֹ֗ול מִתַּ֛חַת רָגְזָ֥ה לְךָ֖ לִקְרַ֣את בֹּואֶ֑ךָ עֹורֵ֨ר לְךָ֤ רְפָאִים֙ כָּל־עַתּ֣וּדֵי אָ֔רֶץ הֵקִים֙ מִכִּסְאֹותָ֔ם כֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֥י גֹויִֽם׃. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 14:9: Ὁ ᾅδης κάτωθεν ἐπικράνθη συναντήσας σοι· συνηγέρθησάν σοι πάντες οἱ γίγαντες οἱ ἄρξαντες τῆς γῆς, οἱ ἐγείραντες ἐκ τῶν θρόνων αὐτῶν πάντας βασιλεῖς ἐθνῶ.. [all the giants who ruled the earth] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/23/14/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ISA14.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew has כָּל־עַתּוּדֵי אָרֶץ, in which עַתּוּד is a word for a male goat, used of leaders. The KJV renders it “chief ones”. The Hebrew verse also has רְפָאִים (“the dead” in the KJV); the Greek has a single phrase and the record does not say which Hebrew word the Greek “giants” answers to. “Giants” names a class of beings; “chief ones” names rank among the living.

summary: Three Hebrew phrases use the same word, רְפָאִים. The KJV renders it “the dead” each time (2:18, 9:18, 21:16). Brenton’s Greek renders it “the earth-born” (γηγενῶν, γηγενεῖς) at 2:18 and 9:18 and “giants” (γιγάντων) at 21:16.
text: KJV Proverbs 2:18: “For her house inclineth unto death, and her paths unto the dead.” KJV Proverbs 9:18: “But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.” KJV Proverbs 21:16: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” Hebrew (WLC) 2:18: כִּ֤י שָׁ֣חָה אֶל־מָ֣וֶת בֵּיתָ֑הּ וְאֶל־רְ֝פָאִ֗ים מַעְגְּלֹתֶֽיהָ׃. Hebrew (WLC) 9:18: וְֽלֹא־יָ֭דַע כִּֽי־רְפָאִ֣ים שָׁ֑ם בְּעִמְקֵ֖י שְׁאֹ֣ול קְרֻאֶֽיהָ׃ פ. Hebrew (WLC) 21:16: אָדָ֗ם תֹּ֭ועֶה מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל רְפָאִ֣ים יָנֽוּחַ׃. Brenton’s Greek 2:18: Ἔθετο γὰρ παρὰ τῷ θανάτῳ τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς, καὶ παρὰ τῷ ᾅδῃ μετὰ τῶν γηγενῶν τοὺς ἄξονας αὐτῆς. [For she has set her house beside death, and her tracks beside Hades, with the earth-born]. Brenton’s Greek 9:18: Ὁ δὲ οὐκ οἶδεν ὅτι γηγενεῖς παρʼ αὐτῇ ὄλλυνται, καὶ ἐπὶ πέταυρον ᾅδου συναντᾷ· [But he does not know that earth-born ones perish beside her, and he comes upon the πέταυρον of Hades]. Brenton’s Greek 21:16: Ἀνὴρ πλανώμενος ἐξ ὁδοῦ δικαιοσύνης, ἐν συναγωγῇ γιγάντων ἀναπαύσεται. [A man who wanders from the way of righteousness will rest in an assembly of giants]. The Greek page prints a different noun: “earth-born” at 2:18 and 9:18, “giants” at 21:16. title: “A prating fool shall fall” (10:10) — the Greek says “he who reproves openly makes peace”
summary: The KJV ends 10:10 with the same words it ends 10:8: “a prating fool shall fall”. Brenton’s Greek ends 10:10 differently from 10:8: “he who reproves with boldness makes peace” (εἰρηνοποιεῖ).
text: KJV Proverbs 10:10: “He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow: but a prating fool shall fall.” KJV Proverbs 10:8: “The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.” Hebrew (WLC) 10:10: קֹ֣רֵֽץ עַ֭יִן יִתֵּ֣ן עַצָּ֑בֶת וֶאֱוִ֥יל פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט׃. Hebrew (WLC) 10:8: חֲכַם־לֵ֭ב יִקַּ֣ח מִצְוֹ֑ת וֶאֱוִ֥יל פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט׃. Brenton’s Greek 10:10: Ὁ ἐννεύων ὀφθαλμοῖς μετὰ δόλου, συνάγει ἀνδράσι λύπας· ὁ δὲ ἐλέγχων μετὰ παῤῥησίας, εἰρηνοποιεῖ. [He who winks with the eyes with guile gathers griefs for men; but he who reproves openly makes peace]. Brenton’s Greek 10:8: Σοφὸς καρδίᾳ δέξεται ἐντολὰς, ὁ δὲ ἄστεγος χείλες σκολιάζων ὑποσκελισθήσεται. At 10:10 the KJV’s outcome is a fool falling; the Greek’s is a reprover making peace.

title: “None of them shall remain or escape” in Egypt — and “a small number that escape the sword shall return”
summary: Jeremiah tells the remnant that all who go to Egypt will die and none will remain or escape (42:17). text: KJV Jeremiah 42:10: “If ye will still abide in this land, then will I build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up: for I repent me of the evil that I have done unto you.” Hebrew (WLC) 42:10: אִם־שֹׁ֤וב תֵּֽשְׁבוּ֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וּבָנִ֤יתִי אֶתְכֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶהֱרֹ֔ס וְנָטַעְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א אֶתֹּ֑ושׁ כִּ֤י נִחַ֙מְתִּי֙ אֶל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי לָכֶֽם׃ Brenton’s Greek 49:10: ἐὰν καθίσαντες καθίσητε ἐν τῇ γῇ ταύτῃ, οἰκοδομήσω ὑμᾶς, καὶ οὐ μὴ καθελῶ, καὶ φυτεύσω ὑμᾶς, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐκτιλῶ, ὅτι ἀναπέπαυμαι ἐπὶ τοῖς κακοῖς οἷς ἐποίησα ὑμῖν. [for I have rested from the evils which I did to you] Brenton’s own English (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/JER49.htm): “for I have ceased from the calamities which I brought upon you”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/42/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER49.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted prints כִּי נִחַמְתִּי אֶל־הָרָעָה, and the KJV renders the verb “I repent me”. The Greek printed uses a verb for resting or ceasing. A statement that the Lord repents is not the same as a statement that he has stopped.
scope: T applies at Jeremiah 42:10 and to the verb only. The record does not say what the Hebrew verb means and makes no claim about whether God repents. The record is limited to this verse. title: “The remnant of the country of Caphtor” and “the remnant of their valley” — Brenton’s Greek prints “the islands” and “the Enakim”
summary: In the KJV of Jeremiah 47:4 the Philistines are the remnant of the country of Caphtor, and 47:5 has Ashkelon cut off “with the remnant of their valley”. The Greek printed has τῶν νήσων, “the islands”, and Ἐνακίμ, a name.
text: KJV Jeremiah 47:4: “Because of the day that cometh to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remaineth: for the Lord will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor.” Hebrew (WLC) 47:4: עַל־הַיֹּ֗ום הַבָּא֙ לִשְׁדֹ֣וד אֶת־כָּל־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְהַכְרִ֤ית לְצֹר֙ וּלְצִידֹ֔ון כֹּ֖ל שָׂרִ֣יד עֹזֵ֑ר כִּֽי־שֹׁדֵ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים שְׁאֵרִ֖ית אִ֥י כַפְתֹּֽור׃ Brenton’s Greek 29:4: ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἐπερχομένῃ τοῦ ἀπολέσαι πάντας τοὺς ἀλλοφύλους· καὶ ἀφανιῶ τὴν Τύρον, καὶ τὴν Σιδῶνα, καὶ πάντας τοὺς καταλοίπους τῆς βοηθείας αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἐξολοθρεύσει Κύριος τοὺς καταλοίπους τῶν νήσων. [for the Lord will utterly destroy the remnant of the islands] KJV Jeremiah 47:5: “Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself?” Hebrew (WLC) 47:5: בָּ֤אָה קָרְחָה֙ אֶל־עַזָּ֔ה נִדְמְתָ֥ה אַשְׁקְלֹ֖ון שְׁאֵרִ֣ית עִמְקָ֑ם עַד־מָתַ֖י תִּתְגֹּודָֽדִי׃    ס Brenton’s Greek 29:5: Ἥκει φαλάκρωμα ἐπὶ Γάζαν, ἀπεῤῥίφη Ἀσκάλων, καὶ οἱ κατάλοιποι Ἐνακίμ. reasoning: In 47:4 the Hebrew edition quoted prints אִי כַפְתּוֹר; the KJV prints the name Caphtor, and the Greek prints a plural noun for islands with no name. In 47:5 the Hebrew edition quoted prints עִמְקָם, “their valley”; the Greek prints Ἐνακίμ, which is a name, and has no valley.

title: “Why then doth their king inherit Gad” — Brenton’s Greek has “Galaad”
summary: The KJV of Jeremiah 49:1 asks why “their king” inherits Gad. The Hebrew edition quoted prints גָּד, Gad. Brenton’s Greek prints Γαλαάδ, Gilead, in that place. The Greek also prints Μελχόλ where the KJV has “their king”; that is a name form and is not the finding.

Why did Melchol take Galaad, and will their people dwell in their cities?] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/49/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER30.htm.

title: “Hazor shall be a dwelling for dragons” — Brenton’s Greek prints “the court” where the KJV has the place name Hazor
summary: The KJV of Jeremiah 49:28 and 49:33 names Hazor. The Greek printed has ἡ αὐλή, “the court” or “the palace”, and titles the oracle “to Kedar, the queen of the court”.
text: KJV Jeremiah 49:28: “Concerning Kedar, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon shall smite, thus saith the Lord; Arise ye, go up to Kedar, and spoil the men of the east.” Hebrew (WLC) 49:28: לְקֵדָ֣ר ׀ וּֽלְמַמְלְכֹ֣ות חָצֹ֗ור אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִכָּה֙ [נְבוּכַדְרֶאצֹּור כ] (נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר ק) מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ אֶל־קֵדָ֔ר וְשָׁדְד֖וּ אֶת־בְּנֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃ Brenton’s Greek 30:23: ΤΗ ΚΗΔΑΡ ΤΗ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΣΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΑΥΛΗΣ, ἫΝ ἘΠΑΤΑΞΕ ΝΑΒΟΥΧΟΔΟΝΟΣΟΡ ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΒΑΒΥΛΩΝΟΣ, οὕτως εἶπε Κύριος, Ἀνάστητε, καὶ ἀνάβητε ἐπὶ Κηδὰρ, καὶ πλήσατε τοὺς υἱοὺς Κεδέμ. text: KJV Jeremiah 49:5: “Behold, I will bring a fear upon thee, saith the Lord God of hosts, from all those that be about thee; and ye shall be driven out every man right forth; and none shall gather up him that wandereth.” KJV Jeremiah 49:6: “And afterward I will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon, saith the Lord.” Hebrew (WLC) 49:6: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת־שְׁב֥וּת בְּנֵֽי־עַמֹּ֖ון נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃    ס Brenton’s Greek 30:21: Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ φέρω φόβον ἐπὶ σὲ, εἶπε Κύριος, ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς περιοίκου σου, καὶ διασπαρήσεσθε ἕκαστος εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ συνάγων. [Behold, I bring fear upon you, says the Lord, from all that is round about you, and you shall be scattered each one before him, and there is none to gather] Brenton’s Greek 30:23: ΤΗ ΚΗΔΑΡ ΤΗ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΣΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΑΥΛΗΣ, ἫΝ ἘΠΑΤΑΞΕ ΝΑΒΟΥΧΟΔΟΝΟΣΟΡ ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΒΑΒΥΛΩΝΟΣ, οὕτως εἶπε Κύριος, Ἀνάστητε, καὶ ἀνάβητε ἐπὶ Κηδὰρ, καὶ πλήσατε τοὺς υἱοὺς Κεδέμ. [To Kedar, the queen of the court, whom Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon struck, thus said the Lord, Arise and go up against Kedar, and fill the sons of Kedem] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/49/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER30.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted closes the Ammon oracle with a return of the captivity (וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵן אָשִׁיב). The Greek page ends the Ammon oracle with the verse about fear on every side and then moves to Kedar. No verse about a return of Ammon is printed.
scope: T applies at Jeremiah 49:6 and to the verses named. title: “The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron” — Brenton’s Greek prints no verses 17:1-4
summary: The KJV and the Hebrew edition quoted have four verses (17:1-4) before “Cursed be the man that trusteth in man”, including “ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever” (17:4). Brenton’s Greek page for the chapter prints no verse numbered 1 to 4; its first label is 5.
text: KJV Jeremiah 17:1: “The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond: it is graven upon the table of their heart, and upon the horns of your altars;” Hebrew (WLC) 17:1: חַטַּ֣את יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּתוּבָ֛ה בְּעֵ֥ט בַּרְזֶ֖ל בְּצִפֹּ֣רֶן שָׁמִ֑יר חֲרוּשָׁה֙ עַל־ל֣וּחַ לִבָּ֔ם וּלְקַרְנֹ֖ות מִזְבְּחֹותֵיכֶֽם׃ KJV Jeremiah 17:4: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.” Brenton’s Greek 17:5: Ἐπικατάρατος ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὃς τὴν ἐλπίδα ἔχει ἐπʼ ἄνθρωπον, καὶ στηρίσει σάρκα βραχίονος αὐτοῦ ἐπʼ αὐτὸν, καὶ ἀπὸ Κυρίου ἀποστῇ ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ. [Cursed is the man who has his hope on man, and will lean on him his arm of flesh, and his heart departs from the Lord] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/17/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER17.htm.

text: KJV Jeremiah 15:6: “Thou hast forsaken me, saith the Lord, thou art gone backward: therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee; I am weary with repenting.” Hebrew (WLC) 15:6: אַ֣תְּ נָטַ֥שְׁתְּ אֹתִ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה אָחֹ֣ור תֵּלֵ֑כִי וָאַ֨ט אֶת־יָדִ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ וָֽאַשְׁחִיתֵ֔ךְ נִלְאֵ֖יתִי הִנָּחֵֽם׃ Brenton’s Greek 15:6: Σὺ ἀπεστράφης με, λέγει Κύριος, ὀπίσω πορεύσῃ· καὶ ἐκτενῶ τὴν χεῖρά μου, καὶ διαφθερῶ σε, καὶ οὐκέτι ἀνήσω αὐτούς· [and I will no longer let them go] Brenton’s own English for the last clause (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/JER15.htm): “and will no more spare them”. title: Removal “because of Manasseh” — and “every one shall die for his own iniquity”
summary: Jeremiah 15:4 gives Manasseh’s deeds in Jerusalem as the reason the people will be sent into all the kingdoms of the earth. Jeremiah 31:29-30 says that in those days the saying about fathers eating sour grapes will end and each will die for his own iniquity.
text: KJV Jeremiah 15:4: “And I will cause them to be removed into all kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem.” KJV 31:29-30: “In those days they shall say no more, The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge. But every one shall die for his own iniquity: every man that eateth the sour grape, his teeth shall be set on edge.” Hebrew (WLC) 15:4: וּנְתַתִּ֣ים [לִזְוָעָה כ] (לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה ק) לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכֹ֣ות הָאָ֑רֶץ בִּ֠גְלַל מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה בֶן־יְחִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ Hebrew (WLC) 31:29-30: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם לֹא־יֹאמְר֣וּ עֹ֔וד אָבֹ֖ות אָ֣כְלוּ בֹ֑סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י בָנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה׃ כִּ֛י אִם־אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֹנֹ֖ו יָמ֑וּת כָּל־הָֽאָדָ֛ם הָאֹכֵ֥ל הַבֹּ֖סֶר תִּקְהֶ֥ינָה שִׁנָּֽיו׃ ס Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 15:4: Καὶ παραδώσω αὐτοὺς εἰς ἀνάγκας πάσαις ταῖς βασιλείαις τῆς γῆς, διὰ Μανασσῆ υἱὸν Ἐζεκίου βασιλέως Ἰούδα, περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Jeremiah 38:29-30: Ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις οὐ μὴ εἴπωσιν, οἱ πατέρες ἔφαγον ὄμφακα, καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες τῶν τέκνων ᾑμωδίασαν. Ἀλλʼ ἢ ἕκαστος ἐν τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀποθανεῖται, καὶ τοῦ φαγόντος τὸν ὄμφακα αἱμωδιάσουσιν οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτοῦ. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER15.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JER31.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/15/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/24/31/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER15.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JER38.htm.
reasoning: 15:4 uses בִּגְלַל (“on account of”) with Manasseh, a king who had died before this word, as the cause of a judgment on the present people. 31:29-30 says the proverb that children suffer for what fathers ate will no longer be said, and that each dies for his own עָוֹן. The Hebrew and the Greek agree with the KJV in both places.
scope: No tag: the Hebrew, the Greek and the KJV agree. The statements can both stand: 31:29-30 is set in “those days”, a later time than 15:4, and the next verses of chapter 15 also charge the present people with their own turning away (15:6). The text does not say that Manasseh’s sin alone caused the removal. The record does not say the passages are in error.

title: Jeroboam’s priests “for the devils” — the Greek says “for the idols and for the vain things”
summary: The KJV says Jeroboam ordained priests for the high places, “for the devils” and for the calves. Brenton’s Greek has “the idols” and “the vain things”, two Greek nouns where the Hebrew has one word (שְׂעִירִים). The same Hebrew word is the one the KJV renders “goats” in Leviticus 16:8.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 2 Chronicles 11:15: “And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:15: וַיַּֽעֲמֶד־לֹו֙ כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים לַבָּמֹ֖ות וְלַשְּׂעִירִ֑ים וְלָעֲגָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃ [and he appointed for himself priests for the high places, and for the seirim, and for the calves that he made]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 11:15: καὶ κατέστησεν ἑαυτῷ ἱερεῖς τῶν ὑψηλῶν καὶ τοῖς εἰδώλοις καὶ τοῖς ματαίοις καὶ τοῖς μόσχοις, ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἱεροβοάμ. [and he appointed for himself priests of the high places, and for the idols, and for the vain things, and for the calves that Jeroboam made]. Brenton English: “And he made for himself priests of the high places, and for the idols, and for the vanities, and for the calves which Jeroboam made.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2CH11.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/11/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2CH11.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2CH11.htm.

New draft supplemental text (reported, unverified):
KJV 2 Chronicles 11:15: “And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:15: וַיַּֽעֲמֶד־לֹו֙ כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים לַבָּמֹ֖ות וְלַשְּׂעִירִ֑ים וְלָעֲגָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃ Brenton’s Greek 11:15: καὶ κατέστησεν ἑαυτῷ ἱερεῖς τῶν ὑψηλῶν καὶ τοῖς εἰδώλοις καὶ τοῖς ματαίοις καὶ τοῖς μόσχοις, ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἱεροβοάμ. [and he appointed for himself priests of the high places, and for the idols, and for the vain things, and for the calves which Jeroboam made] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/11/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2CH11.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The KJV names the second class served by the priests as “devils”, which are beings. The Hebrew word is הַשְּׂעִירִים, the plural noun that Leviticus 16:8 prints for the two goats and that the published Leviticus 17:7 record already sets beside the KJV’s “devils”. Brenton’s Greek here uses two plural nouns, “the idols” and “the vain things”, and does not call them devils. The Hebrew has one word where the Greek has two.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The KJV puts “devils” between the high places and the calves. The Hebrew prints שְׂעִירִים, the same plural noun the KJV renders “goats” at Leviticus 16:8 (see the published record on Leviticus 17:7, which handles the same noun there). The Greek has two Greek nouns in that place, εἰδώλοις (idols) and ματαίοις (vain things). Neither text prints a word for evil spirits.
scope: T applies at 2 Chronicles 11:15, Septuagint only. No Hebrew mistranslation is claimed: the Hebrew noun is the one the KJV renders “goats” elsewhere, but a shared word does not settle its sense here, and it may name beings thought of in goat form. This record compares two printed wordings and does not decide what was worshipped or say that the KJV and Greek disagree about the practice, which both report. It is a sibling of the Leviticus 17:7 record `sacrifices-unto-devils-or-to-vain-things-greek`, at a different verse; the two share no verse. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. title: Jehoiada’s coup: “let none come into the house of the Lord, save the priests” — or captains and the guard brought in?
summary: In 2 Chronicles 23 Jehoiada orders that none enter the house of the Lord except priests and ministering Levites, and the Levites guard the king. In 2 Kings 11 he brings the captains and the guard to himself in the house of the Lord, swears them there, and sets two parts of them to keep its watch.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 2 Chronicles 23:4: “This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you entering on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be porters of the doors;” KJV 23:6: “But let none come into the house of the Lord, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the Lord.” KJV 23:7: “And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whosoever else cometh into the house, he shall be put to death: but be ye with the king when he cometh in, and when he goeth out.” KJV 2 Kings 11:4: “And the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the rulers over hundreds, with the captains and the guard, and brought them to him into the house of the Lord, and made a covenant with them, and took an oath of them in the house of the Lord, and shewed them the king's son.” KJV 11:5: “And he commanded them, saying, This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you that enter in on the sabbath shall even be keepers of the watch of the king's house;” KJV 11:7: “And two parts of all you that go forth on the sabbath, even they shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord about the king.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Chronicles 23:4: זֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֨ית מִכֶּ֜ם בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת לַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְלַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְשֹֽׁעֲרֵ֖י הַסִּפִּֽים׃ [the third of you who come in on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, for gatekeepers of the thresholds]. Hebrew (WLC) 23:6: וְאַל־יָבֹ֣וא בֵית־יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י אִם־הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְהַמְשָׁרְתִ֣ים לַלְוִיִּ֔ם הֵ֥מָּה יָבֹ֖אוּ כִּי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֑מָּה [and let none come into the house of the Lord except the priests and the ministers of the Levites; they shall come in, for they are holy]. Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 11:4: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠שְּׁבִיעִית שָׁלַ֨ח יְהֹויָדָ֜ע וַיִּקַּ֣ח ׀ אֶת־שָׂרֵ֣י [הַמֵּאיֹות כ] (הַמֵּאֹ֗ות ק) לַכָּרִי֙ וְלָ֣רָצִ֔ים וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֛ם אֵלָ֖יו בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה [and in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of the hundreds, for the Carites and the runners, and brought them to him, the house of the Lord; the WLC prints both a written (ketiv) and a read (qere) form of “hundreds”]. Hebrew (WLC) 11:5: הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֤ית מִכֶּם֙ בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת וְשֹׁ֣מְרֵ֔י מִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ [the third of you who come in on the sabbath, and keepers of the watch of the king’s house]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Chronicles 23:6: Καὶ μὴ εἰσελθέτω εἰς οἶκον Κυρίου, ἐὰν μὴ οἱ ἱερεῖς καὶ οἱ Λευῖται καὶ οἱ λειτουργοῦντες τῶν Λευιτῶν [and let none enter the house of the Lord unless the priests and the Levites and the ministers of the Levites]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 4 Kingdoms (2 Kings) 11:4: Καὶ ἐν τῷ ἔτει τῷ ἑβδόμῳ ἀπέστειλεν Ἰωδαὲ, καὶ ἔλαβε τοὺς ἑκατοντάρχους τῶν Χοῤῥὶ καὶ τῶν Ῥασίμ, καὶ ἀπήγαγεν αὐτοὺς πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκον Κυρίου [and Jehoiada sent and took the centurions of the Chorri and the Rasim, and led them to him into the house of the Lord]. The two accounts of the same coup describe the force differently. title: Solomon’s merchants received “linen yarn” — the Greek of 2 Chronicles has no yarn
summary: The KJV says the king’s merchants received “linen yarn” at a price. The Hebrew prints one word, מִקְוֵא, twice, and Brenton’s Greek of 2 Chronicles 1:16 names no goods at all. Brenton’s Greek of 1 Kings 10:28 reads the same place as “from Thekoue”.
text: KJV 2 Chronicles 1:16: “And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price.” Hebrew (WLC) 1:16: וּמֹוצָ֧א הַסּוּסִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּמִקְוֵ֕א סֹחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מִקְוֵ֥א יִקְח֖וּ בִּמְחִֽיר׃ [and the bringing out of the horses that Solomon had from Egypt, and the miqwe; the king’s traders took the miqwe at a price]. Brenton English: “and the charge of the king's merchants for going was as follows, and they traded”. title: “Spake I a word to any of the judges of Israel” — the Greek has “tribe”, as 2 Samuel 7:7 does
summary: The KJV of 1 Chronicles 17:6 has God ask whether he spoke to any of the “judges” of Israel. Brenton’s Greek has “one tribe”. The Hebrew of 2 Samuel 7:7, the parallel verse, has a different noun from 1 Chronicles 17:6: שִׁבְטֵי, “tribes” in the KJV.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 1 Chronicles 17:6: “Wheresoever I have walked with all Israel, spake I a word to any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people, saying, Why have ye not built me an house of cedars?” Hebrew (WLC) 17:6: בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲדָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת־אַחַד֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֛יתִי לִרְעֹ֥ות אֶת־עַמִּ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֛מָּה לֹא־בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 17:6: καὶ ἤμην ἐν σκηνῇ καὶ ἐν καλὺμματι ἐν πᾶσιν οἷς διῆλθον ἐν παντὶ Ἰσραήλ· εἰ λαλῶν ἐλάλησα πρὸς μίαν φυλὴν τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ οἷς ἐνετειλάμην τοῦ ποιμαίνειν τὸν λαόν μου, λέγων, ὅτι οὐκ ᾠκοδομήσατέ μοι οἶκον κέδρινον; Brenton English: “in all places through which I have gone with all Israel: did I ever speak to any one tribe of Israel whom I commanded to feed my people, saying, Why is it that ye have not built me a house of cedar?” KJV 2 Samuel 7:7: “In all the places wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why build ye not me an house of cedar?” Hebrew (WLC) 7:7: בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּכָל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲדָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת־אַחַד֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֗יתִי לִרְעֹ֛ות אֶת־עַמִּ֥י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֛מָּה לֹֽא־בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 7:7: ἐν πᾶσιν οἷς διῆλθον ἐν παντὶ Ἰσραήλ· εἰ λαλῶν ἐλάλησα πρὸς μίαν φυλὴν τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ, ᾧ ἐνετειλάμην ποιμαίνειν τὸν λαόν μου Ἰσραὴλ, λέγων, ἱνατί οὐκ ᾠκοδομήκατέ μοι οἶκον κέδρινον; Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1CH17.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2SA07.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/17/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/10/7/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1CH17.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1CH17.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2SA07.htm.

Preserved draft reasoning:
The KJV of 1 Chronicles 17:6 says “judges”, and the Hebrew prints שֹׁפְטֵי (a plural noun of the root the KJV renders “judge”). Brenton’s Greek of the same verse says “one tribe” (μίαν φυλήν), the reading of the Hebrew in 2 Samuel 7:7 and of Brenton’s Greek there. A plainly different noun, “judges” or “tribes”, stands in the same slot of the parallel speech.

The KJV of the two books has “judges” in one and “tribes” in the other, and the Greek of Chronicles has “tribe”.

title: “I will settle him in mine house and in my kingdom” — the Greek has “his kingdom”, and 2 Samuel 7:16 has “thine house and thy kingdom”
summary: In the KJV God settles David’s son “in mine house and in my kingdom”. The Hebrew says “my kingdom”; Brenton’s Greek says “his kingdom”. In the parallel promise, 2 Samuel 7:16, the house and kingdom are David’s: “thine house and thy kingdom”.

title: David’s count of the Levites: “from the age of thirty years” — or “from twenty years old”?
summary: 1 Chronicles 23:3 numbers the Levites from thirty years old and gives 38,000. Twenty-four verses on, the same chapter says the Levites were numbered from twenty, “by the last words of David”.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 23:3: “Now the Levites were numbered from the age of thirty years and upward: and their number by their polls, man by man, was thirty and eight thousand.” Hebrew (WLC) 23:3: וַיִּסָּֽפְרוּ֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה וַיְהִ֨י מִסְפָּרָ֤ם לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָם֙ לִגְבָרִ֔ים שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁמֹונָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ KJV 1 Chronicles 23:24: “These were the sons of Levi after the house of their fathers; even the chief of the fathers, as they were counted by number of names by their polls, that did the work for the service of the house of the Lord, from the age of twenty years and upward.” Hebrew (WLC) 23:24: אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵֽי־לֵוִי֩ לְבֵ֨ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֜ם רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָבֹ֣ות לִפְקוּדֵיהֶ֗ם בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שֵׁמֹות֙ לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָ֔ם עֹשֵׂה֙ הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָֽעְלָה׃ KJV 1 Chronicles 23:27: “For by the last words of David the Levites were numbered from twenty years old and above:” Hebrew (WLC) 23:27: כִּ֣י בְדִבְרֵ֤י דָוִיד֙ הָאַ֣חֲרֹנִ֔ים הֵ֖מָּה מִסְפַּ֣ר בְּנֵי־לֵוִ֑י מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָֽעְלָה׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 23:3: Καὶ ἠρίθμησαν οἱ Λευῖται ἀπὸ τριακονταετοῦς καὶ ἐπάνω, καὶ ἐγένετο ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτῶν κατὰ κεφαλὴν αὐτῶν εἰς ἄνδρας τριάκοντα καὶ ὀκτὼ χιλιάδας. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 23:27: Ὅτι ἐν τοῖς λόγοις Δαυὶδ τοῖς ἐσχάτοις ἐστὶν ὁ ἀριθμὸς υἱῶν Λευὶ ἀπὸ εἰκοσαετοῦς καὶ ἐπάνω· Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1CH23.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/23/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1CH23.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1CH23.htm.
reasoning: Within one chapter the Levites are numbered from two different ages. Verse 3 gives thirty and a total of 38,000, split in verses 4-5 into 24,000, 6,000, 4,000 and 4,000 (which does add to 38,000). Verses 24 and 27 give twenty, and verse 27 says that is by David’s last words. Numbers 4:3 has thirty, and Numbers 8:24 (in the published `levites-serve-from-thirty-years-old-or-from-twenty-five-greek` and `numbers-levite-age-thresholds`) has twenty-five; this record adds the Chronicles pair, with the figure twenty.
scope: Untagged. The KJV, Hebrew and Greek agree with each other at each verse. The chapter does not say the two counts are the same count: verse 27 introduces a later rule “by the last words of David”, so the chapter may describe two successive reckonings. The record states the difference in age; it does not argue that the text contradicts itself. It makes no claim about Numbers beyond naming it. title: David gathered “thirty thousand” chosen men — Brenton’s Greek has “about seventy thousand”
summary: The KJV and the Hebrew of 2 Samuel 6:1 give thirty thousand chosen men. Brenton’s Greek gives “about seventy thousand” young men.
text: KJV 2 Samuel 6:1: “Again, David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.” Hebrew (WLC) 6:1: וַיֹּ֨סֶף עֹ֥וד דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־כָּל־בָּח֥וּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 6:1: Καὶ συνήγαγεν ἔτι Δαυὶδ πάντα νεανίαν ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, ὡς ἑβδομήκοντα χιλιάδας. Brenton English: “And David again gathered all the young men of Israel, about seventy thousand.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2SA06.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/10/6/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2SA06.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2SA06.htm.

title: Which was the father? “Abiathar” the son of Ahimelech — or “Ahimelech the son of Abiathar”?
summary: 1 Samuel 22:20 makes Abiathar the son of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub. 2 Samuel 8:17 and 1 Chronicles 24:6 make Ahimelech the son of Abiathar; 1 Chronicles 18:16 names the son as Abimelech.
text: KJV 1 Samuel 22:20: “And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.” Hebrew (WLC) 22:20: וַיִּמָּלֵ֣ט בֵּן־אֶחָ֗ד לַאֲחִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ בֶּן־אֲחִט֔וּב וּשְׁמֹ֖ו אֶבְיָתָ֑ר וַיִּבְרַ֖ח אַחֲרֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 22:20: Καὶ διασώζεται υἱὸς εἷς τῷ Ἀβιμέλεχ υἱῷ Ἀχιτὼβ, καὶ ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἀβιάθαρ, καὶ ἔφυγεν ὀπίσω Δαυίδ. KJV 2 Samuel 8:17: “And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Seraiah was the scribe;” Hebrew (WLC) 8:17: וְצָדֹ֧וק בֶּן־אֲחִיט֛וּב וַאֲחִימֶ֥לֶךְ בֶּן־אֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִ֑ים וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה סֹופֵֽר׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 8:17: καὶ Σαδὼκ υἱὸς Ἀχιτὼβ καὶ Ἀχιμέλεχ υἱὸς Ἀβιάθαρ ἱερεῖς· καὶ Σασὰ ὁ γραμματεύς· KJV 1 Chronicles 18:16: “And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Shavsha was scribe;” Hebrew (WLC) 18:16: וְצָדֹ֧וק בֶּן־אֲחִיט֛וּב וַאֲבִימֶ֥לֶךְ בֶּן־אֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִ֑ים וְשַׁוְשָׁ֖א סֹופֵֽר׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 18:16: καὶ Σαδὼκ υἱὸς Ἀχειτὼβ καὶ Αχειμέλεχ υἱὸς Ἀβιάθαρ οἱ ἱερεῖς, καὶ Σουσὰ γραμματεύς, KJV 1 Chronicles 24:6: “And Shemaiah the son of Nethaneel the scribe, one of the Levites, wrote them before the king, and the princes, and Zadok the priest, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and before the chief of the fathers of the priests and Levites: one principal household being taken for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar.” Hebrew (WLC) 24:6: וַֽיִּכְתְּבֵ֡ם שְֽׁמַֽעְיָה֩ בֶן־נְתַנְאֵ֨ל הַסֹּופֵ֜ר מִן־הַלֵּוִ֗י לִפְנֵ֨י הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִים֙ וְצָדֹ֣וק הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וַאֲחִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ בֶּן־אֶבְיָתָ֔ר וְרָאשֵׁי֙ הָֽאָבֹ֔ות לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֑ם בֵּֽית־אָ֣ב אֶחָ֗ד אָחֻז֙ לְאֶלְעָזָ֔ר וְאָחֻ֥ז ׀ אָחֻ֖ז לְאִיתָמָֽר׃  פ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 24:6: Καὶ ἔγραψεν αὐτοὺς Σαμαΐας υἱὸς Ναθαναὴλ ὁ γραμματεὺς ἐκ τοῦ Λευὶ κατέναντι τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ τῶν ἀρχόντων, καὶ Σαδὼκ ὁ ἱερεὺς, καὶ Ἀχιμέλεχ υἱὸς Ἀβιάθαρ, καὶ ἄρχοντες τῶν πατριῶν τῶν ἱερέων καὶ τῶν Λευιτῶν οἴκου πατριᾶς, εἷς εἷς τῷ Ἐλεάζαρ, καὶ εἷς εἷς τῷ Ἰθάμαρ. reasoning: 1 Samuel 22:20 says one son of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub escaped, “and his name was Abiathar”. Later lists of David’s priests (2 Samuel 8:17, 1 Chronicles 18:16, 1 Chronicles 24:6) read “Ahimelech (or Abimelech) the son of Abiathar”, with father and son reversed. The three later verses spell the name two ways in the Hebrew, אֲחִימֶלֶךְ and אֲבִימֶלֶךְ. Brenton’s Greek of all four verses keeps the same order as the Hebrew.

title: The sons of Simeon: six names in Genesis, five in Numbers and 1 Chronicles — and not the same five
summary: Genesis 46:10 names six sons of Simeon. Numbers 26:12 and 1 Chronicles 4:24 each name five, and they differ from each other and from Genesis.
text: KJV Genesis 46:10: “And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman.” Hebrew (WLC) 46:10: וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְעֹ֗ון יְמוּאֵ֧ל וְיָמִ֛ין וְאֹ֖הַד וְיָכִ֣ין וְצֹ֑חַר וְשָׁא֖וּל בֶּן־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽית׃ KJV Numbers 26:12: “The sons of Simeon after their families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites: of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites: of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites:” Hebrew (WLC) 26:12: בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְעֹון֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לִנְמוּאֵ֗ל מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַנְּמ֣וּאֵלִ֔י לְיָמִ֕ין מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיָּמִינִ֑י לְיָכִ֕ין מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיָּכִינִֽי׃ KJV 1 Chronicles 4:24: “The sons of Simeon were, Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul:” Hebrew (WLC) 4:24: בְּנֵ֖י שִׁמְעֹ֑ון נְמוּאֵ֣ל וְיָמִ֔ין יָרִ֖יב זֶ֥רַח שָׁאֽוּל׃ Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/GEN46.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/NUM26.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1CH04.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/1/46/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/26/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/4/.
reasoning: Genesis 46:10: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, Shaul (six). Numbers 26:12 (clans): Nemuel, Jamin, Jachin, Zerah, Shaul (five; Ohad is absent and Zohar is Zerah). 1 Chronicles 4:24: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul (five; Ohad is absent, and Jarib stands where Numbers has Jachin). The list in Chronicles agrees with the Numbers list in four names out of five, and with Genesis in two.
scope: Untagged. Names that differ by a letter or two (Jemuel and Nemuel, Zohar and Zerah, Jarib and Jachin) may be variant spellings or second names of one son; the texts do not say so. Ohad appears only in Genesis 46:10, which may be because he had no clan (Numbers lists clans). The record compares the printed names and counts; it does not say any text is wrong and does not argue from silence about Ohad’s descendants. No Greek text was fetched. title: “Baalah, that is, to Kirjathjearim, which belonged to Judah” — Brenton’s Greek prints “the city of David”
summary: In the KJV of 1 Chronicles 13:6 David and all Israel go up to Baalah, that is Kirjathjearim, to bring up the ark. Brenton’s Greek prints εἰς πόλιν Δαυίδ, “to the city of David”, where the Hebrew edition quoted has the two place names.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 13:6: “And David went up, and all Israel, to Baalah, that is, to Kirjathjearim, which belonged to Judah, to bring up thence the ark of God the Lord, that dwelleth between the cherubims, whose name is called on it.” Hebrew (WLC) 13:6: וַיַּ֨עַל דָּוִ֤יד וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בַּעֲלָ֔תָה אֶל־קִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִיהוּדָ֑ה לְהַעֲלֹ֣ות מִשָּׁ֗ם אֵת֩ אֲרֹ֨ון הָאֱלֹהִ֧ים ׀ יְהוָ֛ה יֹושֵׁ֥ב הַכְּרוּבִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שֵֽׁם׃ Brenton’s Greek 13:6: Καὶ ἀνήγαγεν αὐτὴν Δαυίδ· καὶ πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ ἀνέβη εἰς πόλιν Δαυὶδ, ἣ ἦν τοῦ Ἰούδα, τοῦ ἀναγαγεῖν ἐκεῖθεν τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Κυρίου καθημένου ἐπὶ χερουβὶμ, οὗ ἐπεκλήθη ὄνομα αὐτοῦ. [and David brought it up; and all Israel went up to the city of David, which was Judah’s, to bring up from there the ark of God the Lord] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/13/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1CH13.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted prints בַּעֲלָתָה אֶל־קִרְיַת יְעָרִים, Baalah, to Kiriath-jearim. The Greek printed at the same verse has πόλιν Δαυίδ, the city of David, and does not print either name. The KJV names Baalah and Kirjathjearim; the Greek names the city of David.
scope: T applies at 1 Chronicles 13:6 and only to the place the ark is brought up from. The record does not compare 13:5, where Brenton’s Greek prints “the city of Jarim”, and it does not compare 2 Samuel 6:2. It does not say what the Greek translators or later copyists intended, and it does not say the city of David is Jerusalem. This compares the wording of the texts quoted. It does not show which wording is original. The book is a history written in prose; the comparison is of what the texts print, not of why the writer worded it so. title: “Uzza and Ahio drave the cart” — Brenton’s Greek prints “Oza and his brethren”
summary: The KJV of 1 Chronicles 13:7 names two men driving the new cart, Uzza and Ahio. Brenton’s Greek prints Ὀζὰ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, “Oza and his brothers”, with no second name.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 13:7: “And they carried the ark of God in a new cart out of the house of Abinadab: and Uzza and Ahio drave the cart.” Hebrew (WLC) 13:7: וַיַּרְכִּ֜יבוּ אֶת־אֲרֹ֤ון הָאֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־עֲגָלָ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה מִבֵּ֖ית אֲבִינָדָ֑ב וְעֻזָּ֣א וְאַחְיֹ֔ו נֹהֲגִ֖ים בָּעֲגָלָֽה׃ Brenton’s Greek 13:7: Καὶ ἐπέθηκαν τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐφʼ ἅμαξαν καινὴν ἐξ οἴκου Ἀμιναδάβ· καὶ Ὀζὰ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ ἦγον τὴν ἅμαξαν. [and Oza and his brothers drove the wagon] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/13/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1CH13.htm.

text: KJV 1 Chronicles 27:5: “The third captain of the host for the third month was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, a chief priest: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.” KJV 1 Chronicles 27:34: “And after Ahithophel was Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar: and the general of the king's army was Joab.” Hebrew (WLC) 27:5: שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֤א הַשְּׁלִישִׁי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהֹויָדָ֛ע הַכֹּהֵ֖ן רֹ֑אשׁ וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתֹּ֔ו עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ Hebrew (WLC) 27:34: וְאַחֲרֵ֣י אֲחִיתֹ֗פֶל יְהֹויָדָ֤ע בֶּן־בְּנָיָ֙הוּ֙ וְאֶבְיָתָ֔ר וְשַׂר־צָבָ֥א לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹואָֽב׃  פ Brenton’s Greek 27:5: Ὁ τρίτος τὸν μῆνα τὸν τρίτον Βαναίας ὁ τοῦ Ἰωδαὲ ὁ ἱερεὺς ὁ ἄρχων, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς διαιρέσεως αὐτοῦ εἴκοσι καὶ τέσσαρες χιλιάδες. Brenton’s Greek 27:34: Καὶ μετὰ τοῦτον Ἀχιτόφελ ἐχόμενος Ἰωδαὲ ὁ τοῦ Βαναίου, καὶ Ἀβιάθαρ· καὶ Ἰωὰβ ἀρχιστράτηγος τοῦ βασιλέως. [27:5: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada the priest. 27:34: and after this, Ahithophel, Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar.] Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/27/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1CH27.htm.

title: “Etam, and Ain, Rimmon, and Tochen, and Ashan, five cities” (1 Chronicles 4:32) and “Ain, Remmon, and Ether, and Ashan; four cities” (Joshua 19:7)
summary: The KJV of 1 Chronicles 4:32 lists five of Simeon’s towns (Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, Ashan) and counts them five cities. The KJV of Joshua 19:7 lists four (Ain, Remmon, Ether, Ashan) and counts them four cities.

title: The ark is sent on to Ekron — the Greek names Ascalon (Askelon)
summary: The KJV says the Philistines sent the ark to Ekron (5:10) and that the five lords returned to Ekron (6:16). The Hebrew prints עֶקְרוֹן in both verses. Brenton’s Greek prints Ἀσκάλωνα (Ascalon) in both.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 1 Samuel 5:10: “Therefore they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, as the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, saying, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 5:10: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֛וּ אֶת־אֲרֹ֥ון הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עֶקְרֹ֑ון וַיְהִ֗י כְּבֹ֨וא אֲרֹ֤ון הָאֱלֹהִים֙ עֶקְרֹ֔ון וַיִּזְעֲק֨וּ הָֽעֶקְרֹנִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר הֵסַ֤בּוּ אֵלַי֙ אֶת־אֲרֹון֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַהֲמִיתֵ֖נִי וְאֶת־עַמִּֽי׃ [and they sent the ark of God to Ekron; and it happened, when the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 5:10: Καὶ ἐξαποστέλλουσι τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα· καὶ ἐγενήθη ὡς εἰσῆλθε κιβωτὸς Θεοῦ εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα, καὶ ἐβόησαν οἱ Ἀσκαλωνῖται, λέγοντες, τί ἀπεστρέψατε τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς ἡμᾶς θανατῶσαι ἡμᾶς καὶ τὸν λαὸν ἡμῶν; [and they send away the ark of God to Ascalon; and when the ark of God came into Ascalon, the Ascalonites cried out]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 5:10: “And they send away the ark of God to Ascalon; and it came to pass when the ark of God went into Ascalon, that the men of Ascalon cried out, saying, Why have ye brought back the ark of the God of Israel to us, to kill us and our people?” KJV 1 Samuel 6:16: “And when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 6:16: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה סַרְנֵֽי־פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים רָא֑וּ וַיָּשֻׁ֥בוּ עֶקְרֹ֖ון בַּיֹּ֥ום הַהֽוּא׃    ס [and the five lords of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ekron on that day]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 6:16: Καὶ οἱ πέντε σατράπαι τῶν ἀλλοφύλων ἑώρων, καὶ ἀνέστρεψαν εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ. [and the five satraps of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ascalon on that day]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 6:16: “And the five lords of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ascalon in that day.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA05.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/5/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA05.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA05.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA06.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/6/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA06.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA06.htm.

In both verses the Hebrew reads Ekron and the Greek reads Ascalon, so the Greek tradition sends the ark, and the lords, to a different Philistine city. title: “The judge shall judge him” — the Greek has “they shall pray for him to the Lord”
summary: The KJV has Eli say, “If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him”. The Hebrew is וּפִלְלוֹ אֱלֹהִים. Brenton’s Greek reads καὶ προσεύξονται ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πρὸς Κύριον, “and they shall pray for him to the Lord”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 1 Samuel 2:25: “If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him: but if a man sin against the Lord, who shall intreat for him? Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the Lord would slay them.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 2:25: אִם־יֶחֱטָ֨א אִ֤ישׁ לְאִישׁ֙ וּפִֽלְלֹ֣ו אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאִ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ יֶֽחֱטָא־אִ֔ישׁ מִ֖י יִתְפַּלֶּל־לֹ֑ו וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁמְעוּ֙ לְקֹ֣ול אֲבִיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־חָפֵ֥ץ יְהוָ֖ה לַהֲמִיתָֽם׃ [if a man sins against a man, God [or: judges] will judge for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 2:25: Ἐὰν ἁμαρτάνων ἁμάρτῃ ἀνὴρ εἰς ἄνδρα, καὶ προσεύξονται ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πρὸς Κύριον· καὶ ἐὰν τῷ Κυρίῳ ἁμάρτῃ, τίς προσεύξεται ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ; Καὶ οὐκ ἤκουον τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν, ὅτι βουλόμενος ἐβούλετο Κύριος διαφθεῖραι αὐτούς. [if a man sins against a man, they shall pray for him to the Lord; and if he sins against the Lord, who shall pray for him?]. title: Why the men of Bethshemesh were smitten — the Greek adds “the sons of Jechonias were not pleased”
summary: The KJV says the Lord smote the men of Bethshemesh “because they had looked into the ark of the Lord”. The Hebrew says כִּי רָאוּ בַּאֲרוֹן יְהוָה, “because they saw into the ark of the LORD”. Brenton’s Greek opens with a different clause: οὐκ ἠσμένισαν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰεχονίου ἐν τοῖς ἀνδράσι Βαιθσαμύς, “the sons of Jechonias were not pleased with the men of Bethshemesh”, and then adds “because they saw the ark of the Lord”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 1 Samuel 6:19: “And he smote the men of Bethshemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even he smote of the people fifty thousand and threescore and ten men: and the people lamented, because the Lord had smitten many of the people with a great slaughter.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 6:19: וַיַּ֞ךְ בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י רָאוּ֙ בַּאֲרֹ֣ון יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֤ךְ בָּעָם֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽתְאַבְּל֣וּ הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּעָ֖ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדֹולָֽה ׃ [and he struck among the men of Bethshemesh because they saw into the ark of the LORD, and he struck among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 6:19: Καὶ οὐκ ἠσμένισαν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰεχονίου ἐν τοῖς ἀνδράσι Βαιθσαμὺς, ὅτι εἶδαν κιβωτὸν Κυρίου· καὶ ἐπάταξεν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἑβδομήκοντα ἄνδρας, καὶ πεντήκοντα χιλιάδας ἀνδρῶν· καὶ ἐπένθησεν ὁ λαός, ὅτι ἐπάταξε Κύριος ἐν τῷ λαῷ πληγὴν μεγάλην σφόδρα. [and the sons of Jechonias were not pleased among the men of Bethshemesh because they saw the ark of the Lord; and he struck among them seventy men and fifty thousand men]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 6:19: “And the sons of Jechonias were not pleased with the men of Bæthsamys, because they saw the ark of the Lord; and the Lord smote among them seventy men, and fifty thousand men: and the people mourned, because the Lord had inflicted on the people a very great plague.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA06.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/6/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA06.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA06.htm.

Preserved draft reasoning:
In the Hebrew the cause of the slaughter is given in a single clause. In the Greek there is an additional group, the sons of Jechonias, who are displeased with the Bethshemesh men for seeing the ark, and the plague falls “among them”. A reader of the Greek has a named family in the story whom the Hebrew does not name. The number is the same in both: seventy men and fifty thousand men.

The Hebrew edition quoted prints a verb of smiting with the men of Beth-shemesh as object, followed by “because they saw the ark of the Lord”. The Greek printed at the same verse has the sons of Jeconiah as subject of a verb that is not smiting, and the smiting comes in a later clause. The KJV follows the Hebrew; the Greek prints a different first clause.

title: David leaves Keilah with “about six hundred” — the Greek has “about four hundred”
summary: The KJV says David and his men, “which were about six hundred”, left Keilah. The Hebrew prints כְּשֵׁשׁ־מֵאוֹת אִישׁ, “about six hundred men”. Brenton’s Greek prints ὡς τετρακόσιοι, “about four hundred”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 1 Samuel 23:13: “Then David and his men, which were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go. And it was told Saul that David was escaped from Keilah; and he forbare to go forth.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 23:13: וַיָּקָם֩ דָּוִ֨ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו כְּשֵׁשׁ־מֵאֹ֣ות אִ֗ישׁ וַיֵּצְאוּ֙ מִקְּעִלָ֔ה וַיִּֽתְהַלְּכ֖וּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְהַלָּ֑כוּ וּלְשָׁא֣וּל הֻגַּ֗ד כִּֽי־נִמְלַ֤ט דָּוִד֙ מִקְּעִילָ֔ה וַיֶּחְדַּ֖ל לָצֵֽאת׃ [and David arose, and his men, about six hundred men, and they went out from Keilah and went wherever they could go]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 23:13: Καὶ ἀνέστη Δαυὶδ καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὡς τετρακόσιοι, καὶ ἐξῆλθον ἐκ Κεϊλὰ, καὶ ἐπορεύοντο οὗ ἐὰν ἐπορεύοντο· καὶ τῷ Σαοὺλ ἀπηγγέλη, ὅτι διασέσωσται Δαυὶδ ἐκ Κεϊλὰ, καὶ ἀνῆκε τοῦ ἐλθεῖν. title: “The king of Israel is come out to seek a flea” — the Greek has “to seek my life”
summary: The KJV has David say the king of Israel “is come out to seek a flea”. The Hebrew is לְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־פַּרְעֹשׁ אֶחָד, “to seek one flea”. Brenton’s Greek reads ζητεῖν ψυχήν μου, “to seek my life”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 1 Samuel 26:20: “Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 26:20: וְעַתָּ֗ה אַל־יִפֹּ֤ל דָּֽמִי֙ אַ֔רְצָה מִנֶּ֖גֶד פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָצָ֞א מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֣שׁ אֶחָ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִרְדֹּ֥ף הַקֹּרֵ֖א בֶּהָרִֽים׃ [for the king of Israel has come out to seek one flea, as one pursues the partridge on the mountains]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 26:20: Καὶ νῦν μὴ πέσοι τὸ αἷμά μου ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἐξεναντίας προσώπου Κυρίου, ὅτι ἐξελήλυθεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ ζητεῖν ψυχήν μου, καθὼς καταδιώκει ὁ νυκτικόραξ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι. [for the king of Israel has come out to seek my life, as the night-raven pursues in the mountains]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 26:20: “And now let not my blood fall to the ground before the Lord, for the king of Israel has come forth to seek thy life, as the night hawk pursues its prey in the mountains..” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA26.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/26/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA26.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA26.htm.

title: David has been with Achish “these days, or these years” — the Greek has “this second year”
summary: The KJV has Achish say David “hath been with me these days, or these years”. The Hebrew is זֶה יָמִים אוֹ־זֶה שָׁנִים, “these days or these years”. Brenton’s Greek reads ἡμέρας τοῦτο δεύτερον ἔτος, “days, this second year”.
text:

KJV 1 Samuel 29:3: “Then said the princes of the Philistines, What do these Hebrews here? [he has been with us days, this second year, and I have found nothing in him from the day he fell upon me until this day]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 29:3: “And the lords of the Philistines said, Who are these that pass by? title: Elijah “stretched himself upon the child”; the soul “came into him again” — Brenton’s Greek says he breathed on the child and the child cried out

[And he breathed on the child three times, and called on the Lord … let the soul of this child turn back into him]. KJV 1 Kings 17:22: “And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Kings 17:22: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה בְּקֹ֣ול אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַתָּ֧שָׁב נֶֽפֶשׁ־הַיֶּ֛לֶד עַל־קִרְבֹּ֖ו וַיֶּֽחִי׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Kings 17:22: Καὶ ἐγένετο οὕτως· καὶ ἀνεβόησε τὸ παιδάριον. summary: KJV 1 Kings 2:5 says Joab shed “the blood of war in peace” and “put the blood of war upon his girdle”. The Hebrew prints דְּמֵי־מִלְחָמָה twice; Brenton’s Greek prints “the bloods of war” the first time and αἷμα ἀθῶον, “innocent blood”, the second.
text: KJV 1 Kings 2:5: “Moreover thou knowest also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, unto Abner the son of Ner, and unto Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war upon his girdle that was about his loins, and in his shoes that were on his feet.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Kings 2:5: וְגַ֣ם אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֡עְתָּ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁר־עָ֨שָׂה לִ֜י יֹואָ֣ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה לִשְׁנֵֽי־שָׂרֵ֣י צִבְאֹ֣ות יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל לְאַבְנֵ֨ר בֶּן־נֵ֜ר וְלַעֲמָשָׂ֤א בֶן־יֶ֙תֶר֙ וַיַּ֣הַרְגֵ֔ם וַיָּ֥שֶׂם דְּמֵֽי־מִלְחָמָ֖ה בְּשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיִּתֵּ֞ן דְּמֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֗ה בַּחֲגֹֽרָתֹו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמָתְנָ֔יו וּֽבְנַעֲלֹ֖ו אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלָֽיו׃ [… and he set blood-of-war in peace, and he put blood-of-war on his girdle that was on his loins and on his sandal that was on his foot]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Kings 2:5: Καί γε σὺ ἔγνως ὅσα ἐποίησέ μοι Ἰωὰβ υἱὸς Σαρουίας, ὅσα ἐποίησε τοῖς δυσὶν ἄρχουσι τῶν δυνάμεων Ἰσραὴλ, τῷ Ἀβεννὴρ υἱῷ Νὴρ, καὶ τῷ Ἀμεσσαῒ υἱῷ Ἰεθὲρ, καὶ ἀπέκτεινεν αὐτοὺς, καὶ ἔταξε τὰ αἵματα πολέμου ἐν εἰρήνῃ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αἷμα ἀθῶον ἐν τῇ ζώνῃ αὐτοῦ τῇ ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν τῷ ὑποδήματι αὐτοῦ τῷ ἐν τῷ ποδὶ αὐτοῦ. [… and he ordered the bloods of war in peace, and put innocent blood on his girdle … ]. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1KI02.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/2/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI02.htm.

title: In the KJV Jeroboam comes and speaks to Rehoboam (12:3, 12:12) — Brenton’s Greek names only the people
summary: KJV 1 Kings 12:3 and 12:12 name Jeroboam among those who came and spoke to Rehoboam; KJV 12:20 says all Israel later heard that “Jeroboam was come again”. Brenton’s Greek prints no verse 2 and says only that “the people” spoke (12:3) and “all Israel” came (12:12); at 12:20 it says Jeroboam “returned out of Egypt”.
text: KJV 1 Kings 12:3: “That they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came, and spake unto Rehoboam, saying,” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Kings 12:3: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ וַיִּקְרְאוּ־לֹ֔ו [וַיָּבֹאוּ כ] (וַיָּבֹ֥א ק) יָרָבְעָ֖ם וְכָל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Kings 12:3: Καὶ ἐλάλησεν ὁ λαὸς πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα Ῥοβοὰμ, λέγοντες, [And the people spoke to king Rehoboam, saying,]. KJV 1 Kings 12:12: “So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, Come to me again the third day.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Kings 12:12: [וַיָּבֹו כ] (וַיָּבֹ֨וא ק) יָרָבְעָ֧ם וְכָל־הָעָ֛ם אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֖ם בַּיֹּ֣ום הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שׁ֥וּבוּ אֵלַ֖י בַּיֹּ֥ום הַשְּׁלִישִֽׁי׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Kings 12:12: Καὶ παρεγένοντο πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα Ῥοβοὰμ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ, καθότι ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς ὁ βασιλεὺς, λέγων, ἀναστράφητε πρὸς μὲ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ. [And all Israel came to king Rehoboam on the third day …]. KJV 1 Kings 12:20: “And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come again, that they sent and called him unto the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.” Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Kings 12:20: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤκουσε πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι ἀνέκαμψεν Ἱεροβοὰμ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν καὶ ἐκάλεσαν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν, καὶ ἐβασίλευσαν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ Ἰσραήλ· καὶ οὐκ ἦν ὀπίσω οἴκου Δαυὶδ πάρεξ σκήπτρου Ἰούδα καὶ Βενιαμὶν μόνοι. [… that Jeroboam had returned out of Egypt …]. The Brenton Greek page prints verse 1 and then verse 3; it prints no verse 2 (the Hebrew verse 2 says Jeroboam heard in Egypt, where he had fled from Solomon). reasoning: In the KJV Jeroboam is called from Egypt and speaks to Rehoboam at Shechem (12:3) and returns on the third day (12:12), yet 12:20 says all Israel, after the people had departed to their tents, “heard that Jeroboam was come again” and then made him king. The KJV passages could stand together if “come again” at 12:20 means a later arrival from Egypt, which the text does not report; this record does not say Jeroboam was or was not at the meeting. title: Rehoboam gathered “an hundred and fourscore thousand” — Brenton’s Greek of 1 Kings says 120,000
