title: Elijah’s word: “dogs lick thy blood” — Brenton’s Greek adds swine and “the harlots shall wash themselves in thy blood”
summary: KJV 1 Kings 21:19 foretells only that dogs shall lick Ahab’s blood where they licked Naboth’s. The Hebrew prints הַכְּלָבִים only; Brenton’s Greek prints “the swine and the dogs” for Naboth’s blood and adds καὶ αἱ πόρναι λούσονται ἐν τῷ αἵματί σου, “and the harlots shall wash themselves in thy blood”.
text: KJV 1 Kings 21:19: “And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord, In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Kings 21:19: וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲרָצַ֖חְתָּ וְגַם־יָרָ֑שְׁתָּ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּמְקֹ֗ום אֲשֶׁ֨ר לָקְק֤וּ הַכְּלָבִים֙ אֶת־דַּ֣ם נָבֹ֔ות יָלֹ֧קּוּ הַכְּלָבִ֛ים אֶת־דָּמְךָ֖ גַּם־אָֽתָּה׃ [… in the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth the dogs shall lick your blood, even you]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek, printed as chapter 20) 1 Kings 21:19: Καὶ λαλήσεις πρὸς αὐτὸν, λέγων, τάδε λέγει Κύριος, ὡς σὺ ἐφόνευσας καὶ ἐκληρονόμησας, διὰ τοῦτο τάδε λέγει Κύριος, ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ ᾧ ἔλειξαν αἱ ὗες καὶ οἱ κύνες τὸ αἷμα Ναβουθαὶ, ἐκεῖ λείξουσιν οἱ κύνες τὸ αἷμά σου, καὶ αἱ πόρναι λούσονται ἐν τῷ αἵματί σου. [… in every place where the swine and the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, there the dogs shall lick your blood, and the harlots shall wash in your blood]. KJV 1 Kings 22:38: “And one washed the chariot in the pool of Samaria; and the dogs licked up his blood; and they washed his armour; according unto the word of the Lord which he spake.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Kings 22:38: וַיִּשְׁטֹ֨ף אֶת־הָרֶ֜כֶב עַ֣ל ׀ בְּרֵכַ֣ת שֹׁמְרֹ֗ון וַיָּלֹ֤קּוּ הַכְּלָבִים֙ אֶת־דָּמֹ֔ו וְהַזֹּנֹ֖ות רָחָ֑צוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Kings 22:38: Καὶ ἀπένιψαν τὸ ἅρμα ἐπὶ τὴν κρήνην Σαμαρείας· καὶ ἐξέλιξαν αἱ ὗες καὶ οἱ κύνες τὸ αἷμα, καὶ αἱ πόρναι ἐλούσαντο ἐν τῷ αἵματι, κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμα Κυρίου ὃ ἐλάλησε.. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1KI21.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/21/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI20.htm. 22:38 fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/22/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI22.htm.
reasoning: The KJV and Hebrew of 21:19 name dogs alone and say nothing of harlots. The Greek edition names swine and dogs for Naboth’s blood and adds the harlots washing in Ahab’s blood. The Hebrew of 22:38 reports that the harlots washed and the Greek of 22:38 reports that swine, dogs and harlots did, so the Greek of 21:19 matches the report in the Greek of 22:38.
scope: T applies at 1 Kings 21:19 only and compares what the foretelling prints. A separate record already compares 1 Kings 22:38 (“they washed his armour” in the KJV against harlots washing in the Hebrew and Greek); this one concerns the earlier verse, where the Hebrew has no harlots. It does not say the Greek foretelling was added after the event, which text is original, or that the KJV 21:19 and 22:38 conflict. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. title: Solomon sends Benaiah at once — Brenton’s Greek prints an exchange between Solomon and Joab first
summary: In the KJV of 1 Kings 2:29 Solomon hears that Joab is at the altar and sends Benaiah with the words “Go, fall upon him”. Brenton’s Greek prints a message from Solomon to Joab, “What has happened to you, that you have fled to the altar?”, and Joab’s answer, “Because I was afraid of you”, before Benaiah is sent.
text: KJV 1 Kings 2:29: “And it was told king Solomon that Joab was fled unto the tabernacle of the Lord; and, behold, he is by the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, fall upon him.” Hebrew (WLC) 2:29: וַיֻּגַּ֞ד לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כִּ֣י נָ֤ס יֹואָב֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה אֵ֣צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת־בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהֹויָדָ֛ע לֵאמֹ֖ר לֵ֥ךְ פְּגַע־בֹּֽו׃ Brenton’s Greek 2:29: Καὶ ἀπηγγέλη τῷ Σαλωμὼν, λέγοντες, ὅτι πέφευγεν Ἰωὰβ εἰς τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Κυρίου, καὶ ἰδοὺ κατέχει τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου· καὶ ἀπέστειλε Σαλωμὼν ὁ βασιλεὺς πρὸς Ἰωὰβ, λέγων, τί γέγονέ σοι, ὅτι πέφευγας εἰς τὸ θυσιαστήριον; καὶ εἶπεν Ἰωὰβ, ὅτι ἐφοβήθην ἀπὸ προσώπου σου, καὶ ἔφυγον πρὸς Κύριον· καὶ ἀπέστειλε Σαλωμὼν τὸν Βαναίου υἱὸν Ἰωδαὲ, λέγων, πορεύου καὶ ἄνελε αὐτὸν, καὶ θάψον αὐτόν. And Joab said, Because I was afraid of you, and I fled to the Lord; and Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, Go and kill him, and bury him] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1KI02.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/2/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI02.htm.

The Greek printed at the same verse puts a question from Solomon and an answer from Joab between the report and the sending. The KJV gives Joab’s reply only later, to Benaiah, in 2:30 (“Nay; but I will die here”). Joab’s stated reason, fear of Solomon, and Solomon’s question to him appear in the Greek verse and in neither the Hebrew nor the KJV.

title: Jeroboam’s mother — Brenton’s Greek adds at 12:24b that she was “a harlot”
summary: The KJV of 1 Kings 11:26 calls Jeroboam’s mother Zeruah, “a widow woman”. Brenton’s Greek of 11:26 also has a widow, but the Greek addition printed after 12:24 (12:24b) names her Sarira and calls her γυνὴ πόρνη, “a harlot”.
text: KJV 1 Kings 11:26: “And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon's servant, whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow woman, even he lifted up his hand against the king.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:26: וְיָרָבְעָם֩ בֶּן־נְבָ֨ט אֶפְרָתִ֜י מִן־הַצְּרֵדָ֗ה וְשֵׁ֤ם אִמֹּו֙ צְרוּעָה֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אַלְמָנָ֔ה עֶ֖בֶד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיָּ֥רֶם יָ֖ד בַּמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ Brenton’s Greek 11:26: Καὶ Ἱεροβοὰμ υἱὸς Ναβὰτ ὁ Ἐφραθὶ ἐκ τῆς Σαριρὰ, υἱὸς γυναικὸς χήρας, δοῦλος Σαλωμών. [and Jeroboam son of Nabat the Ephrathite, from Sarira, son of a widow woman, servant of Solomon] Second place. KJV 1 Kings 12:24: “Thus saith the Lord, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me. They hearkened therefore to the word of the Lord, and returned to depart, according to the word of the Lord.” Hebrew (WLC) 12:24: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה לֹֽא־תַעֲלוּ֩ וְלֹא־תִלָּ֨חֲמ֜וּן עִם־אֲחֵיכֶ֣ם בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּבוּ אִ֣ישׁ לְבֵיתֹ֔ו כִּ֧י מֵאִתִּ֛י נִהְיָ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֥בוּ לָלֶ֖כֶת כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ ס Brenton’s Greek 12:24b: Καὶ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὄρους Ἐφραὶμ δοῦλος τῷ Σαλωμὼν, καὶ ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἱεροβοὰμ, καὶ ὄνομα τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Σαριρὰ, γυνὴ πόρνη· καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν Σαλωμὼν εἰς ἄρχοντα σκυτάλης ἐπὶ ἄρσεις οἴκου Ἰωσήφ· καὶ ᾠκοδόμησε τῷ Σαλωμὼν τὴν Σαριρὰ τὴν ἐν ὄρει Ἐφραίμ· καὶ ἦσαν αὐτῷ τριακόσια ἅρματα ἵππων· οὗτος ᾠκοδόμησε τὴν ἄκραν ἐν ταῖς ἄρσεσιν οἴκου Ἐφραὶμ, οὗτος συνέκλεισε τὴν πόλιν Δαυὶδ, καὶ ἦν ἐπαιρόμενος ἐπὶ τὴν βασιλείαν· [and there was a man from mount Ephraim, a servant to Solomon, and his name was Jeroboam, and the name of his mother was Sarira, a woman, a harlot] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1KI11.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/11/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI11.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1KI12.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/12/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI12.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted names his mother Zeruah and calls her אִשָּׁה אַלְמָנָה, a widow. Brenton’s Greek at 11:26 agrees she is a widow, though it names the place Sarira. Brenton’s Greek at 12:24b, in the added section printed after 12:24, gives the mother’s name as Sarira and describes her as γυνὴ πόρνη. The two Greek passages therefore print “widow” and “harlot” of the same woman. A widow can also have been a harlot, so the two descriptions are not shown to be incompatible by wording alone; the record sets out what each passage prints.
scope: T applies at the Greek addition 12:24b only; 11:26 is context. A widow can also have been a harlot; the record does not claim the two descriptions conflict.

title: Ahab rises and goes down to the vineyard — Brenton’s Greek adds that he first tore his clothes and put on sackcloth
summary: In the KJV of 1 Kings 21:16 Ahab hears that Naboth is dead and goes straight down to the vineyard. Brenton’s Greek (its chapter 20) prints that he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth, and only after that went down.
text: KJV 1 Kings 21:16: “And it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab rose up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.” Hebrew (WLC) 21:16: וַיְהִ֛י כִּשְׁמֹ֥עַ אַחְאָ֖ב כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת נָבֹ֑ות וַיָּ֣קָם אַחְאָ֗ב לָרֶ֛דֶת אֶל־כֶּ֛רֶם נָבֹ֥ות הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֖י לְרִשְׁתֹּֽו׃ ס Brenton’s Greek 20:16: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤκουσεν Ἀχαὰβ ὅτι τέθνηκε Ναβουθαὶ ὁ Ἰεζραηλίτης, καὶ διέῤῥηξε τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, καὶ περιεβάλετο σάκκον· καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ ταῦτα, καὶ ἀνέστη καὶ κατέβη Ἀχαὰβ εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα Ναβουθαὶ τοῦ Ἰεζραηλίτου κληρονομῆσαι αὐτόν. [and it came to pass, when Achaab heard that Naboth the Jezreelite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth; and it came to pass after this, he rose up and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1KI21.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/21/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI20.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has Ahab hear of Naboth’s death and rise to go down. The Greek printed at the same verse puts an act of mourning, tearing his clothes and putting on sackcloth, on hearing the news. The KJV reports tearing and sackcloth at 21:27, after Elijah’s word, as the act that follows the judgment. The Greek at 21:16 reports tearing and sackcloth at an earlier moment, on hearing of Naboth’s death.

title: “full ears of corn in the husk thereof” — Brenton’s Greek has “cakes of figs”
summary: The man from Baalshalisha brings Elisha twenty barley loaves and, in the KJV, “full ears of corn in the husk thereof”. The Hebrew word beside the loaves is וְכַרְמֶל בְּצִקְלֹנוֹ; Brenton’s Greek prints καὶ παλάθας, “and cakes of figs”, and has nothing like “in the husk”.

Preserved draft text:

title: Sennacherib’s sons escaped into “the land of Armenia” — the Hebrew prints “the land of Ararat”
summary: In both 2 Kings 19:37 and Isaiah 37:38 the KJV says Adrammelech and Sharezer escaped “into the land of Armenia”. The Hebrew prints אֶרֶץ אֲרָרָט, “the land of Ararat”, a different name, and Brenton’s Greek of 2 Kings prints Ararath. Brenton’s Greek of 2 Kings 19:37 also prints Ἀραράθ, so the Greek agrees with the Hebrew against the KJV there. At Isaiah 37:38 Brenton instead prints Ἀρμενίαν (Armenia), agreeing with the KJV; only the Hebrew differs there.

title: “A conspiracy of her prophets” — the Brenton Greek says her princes
summary: The KJV says “There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion”. The Hebrew prints קֶשֶׁר נְבִיאֶיהָ, “conspiracy of her prophets”. Brenton’s Greek prints οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι, “those who lead”, which Brenton’s English renders “princes”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Ezekiel 22:25: “There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion ravening the prey; they have devoured souls; they have taken the treasure and precious things; they have made her many widows in the midst thereof.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 22:25: קֶ֤שֶׁר נְבִיאֶ֙יהָ֙ בְּתֹוכָ֔הּ כַּאֲרִ֥י שֹׁואֵ֖ג טֹ֣רֵֽף טָ֑רֶף נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָכָ֗לוּ חֹ֤סֶן וִיקָר֙ יִקָּ֔חוּ אַלְמְנֹותֶ֖יהָ הִרְבּ֥וּ בְתֹוכָֽהּ׃ [a conspiracy of her prophets in her midst, like a roaring lion tearing prey, they devoured life, took treasure and precious things, made her widows many in her midst]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 22:25: Ἧς οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ὡς λέοντες ὠρυόμενοι ἁρπάζοντες ἁρπάγματα, ψυχὰς κατεσθίοντες ἐν δυναστείᾳ, καὶ τιμὰς λαμβάνοντες· καὶ χῆραί σου ἐπληθύνθησαν ἐν μέσῳ σου. Brenton English Ezekiel 22:25: “whose princes in the midst of her are as roaring lions seizing prey, devouring souls by oppression, and taking bribes; and thy widows are multiplied in the midst of thee.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK22.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/22/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK22.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK22.htm.

title: “The east country … the desert” — the Brenton Greek prints Galilee and Arabia
summary: The KJV says the waters “issue out toward the east country, and go down into the desert”. title: Ezekiel bears his baggage “upon thy shoulders” — the Brenton Greek has him lifted up on others’ shoulders
summary: In the sign of the exile the KJV has Ezekiel carry his baggage on his own shoulder through the hole in the wall (12:6, 12:7). Brenton’s Greek prints ἐπʼ ὤμων ἀναληφθήσῃ, “thou shalt be taken up on shoulders”, and ἐπʼ ὤμων ἀνελήφθην, “I was taken up on shoulders”.

Preserved draft text:
KJV Ezekiel 12:6: “In their sight shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulders, and carry it forth in the twilight: thou shalt cover thy face, that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 12:6: לְעֵ֨ינֵיהֶ֜ם עַל־כָּתֵ֤ף תִּשָּׂא֙ בָּעֲלָטָ֣ה תֹוצִ֔יא פָּנֶ֣יךָ תְכַסֶּ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תִרְאֶ֖ה אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־מֹופֵ֥ת נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ [before their eyes you shall carry it on a shoulder, you shall bring it out in the dark; you shall cover your face, and not see the ground]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ezekiel 12:6: ἐπʼ ὤμων ἀναληφθήσῃ, καὶ κεκρυμμένος ἐξελεύσῃ, τὸ πρόσωπόν σου συγκαλύψεις, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδῃς τὴν γῆν, διότι τέρας δέδωκά σε τῷ οἴκῳ Ἰσραήλ. Brenton English Ezekiel 12:6: “thou shalt be lifted up on men's shoulders, and shalt go forth in secret: thou shalt cover thy face, and shalt not see the ground: because I have made thee a sign to the house of Israel.” KJV Ezekiel 12:7: “And I did so as I was commanded: I brought forth my stuff by day, as stuff for captivity, and in the even I digged through the wall with mine hand; I brought it forth in the twilight, and I bare it upon my shoulder in their sight.” Hebrew (WLC) Ezekiel 12:7: וָאַ֣עַשׂ כֵּן֮ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צֻוֵּיתִי֒ כֵּ֠לַי הֹוצֵ֜אתִי כִּכְלֵ֤י גֹולָה֙ יֹומָ֔ם וּבָעֶ֛רֶב חָתַֽרְתִּי־לִ֥י בַקִּ֖יר בְּיָ֑ד בָּעֲלָטָ֥ה הֹוצֵ֛אתִי עַל־כָּתֵ֥ף נָשָׂ֖אתִי לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃  פ [and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hand; in the dark I brought it out, I carried it on a shoulder before their eyes]. Brenton English Ezekiel 12:7: “And I did thus according to all that he commanded me; and I carried forth my baggage for captivity by day, and in the evening I dug through the wall for myself, and went out secretly; I was taken up on men's shoulders before them.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK12.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/12/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK12.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK12.htm.

[And I did so according to all that he commanded me; and I carried out vessels of captivity by day, and in the evening I dug through the wall for myself, and went out hidden; I was taken up on shoulders before them] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK12.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/12/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK12.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The Hebrew verbs are active: you carry, I carried. The Greek verbs are passive: you will be taken up, I was taken up. Brenton’s English renders the Greek with “on men’s shoulders” and has the prophet lifted. In the KJV the prophet carries the stuff; in the Greek he is carried.

title: “The king shall mourn” — the Brenton Greek has no king in the verse
summary: The KJV says “The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation”. title: “At even my wife died” — the Brenton Greek does not mention her death
summary: The KJV says Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning and “at even my wife died”. The Hebrew prints וַתָּמָת אִשְׁתִּי בָּעָרֶב, “and my wife died in the evening”. Brenton English Ezekiel 24:18: “And I spoke to the people in the morning, as he commanded me in the evening, and I did in the morning as it was commanded me.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK24.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/24/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK24.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/EZK24.htm.

title: “The twelfth year … the tenth month” — the Brenton Greek says the tenth year, the twelfth month

title: Waters “to the ankles … to the knees” — the Brenton Greek has no ankles and says thighs
summary: In the vision of the river from the temple the KJV measures the depth four times: ankles (47:3), knees, loins (47:4) and a river to swim in (47:5). title: “My servant the BRANCH” in the Hebrew — “my servant Anatole” (the East, or Rising) in the Greek
summary:
The KJV prints “my servant the BRANCH” for the Hebrew צֶמַח. Brenton’s Greek prints Ἀνατολήν, “rising” or “the East”, and Brenton’s English margin points to Luke 1:78.

Additional retained draft evidence/qualification:
The KJV says Joshua’s fellows are men wondered at. The Hebrew is אַנְשֵׁי מוֹפֵת, “men of a sign”. Brenton’s Greek is ἄνδρες τερατοσκόποι, which Brenton renders “diviners”.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Zechariah 3:8: “Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the Branch.” Hebrew (WLC) Zechariah 3:8: שְֽׁמַֽע־נָ֞א יְהֹושֻׁ֣עַ ׀ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּדֹ֗ול אַתָּה֙ וְרֵעֶ֙יךָ֙ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֣ים לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־אַנְשֵׁ֥י מֹופֵ֖ת הֵ֑מָּה כִּֽי־הִנְנִ֥י מֵבִ֛יא אֶת־עַבְדִּ֖י צֶֽמַח׃ [for behold I am bringing my servant, Branch]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Zechariah 3:8: Ἄκουε δὴ Ἰησοῦ ὁ ἱερεὺς ὁ μέγας, σὺ καὶ οἱ πλησίον σου οἱ καθήμενοι πρὸ προσώπου, διότι ἄνδρες τερατοσκόποι εἰσὶ, διότι ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἄγω τὸν δοῦλόν μου Ἀνατολήν. [for behold I am bringing my servant, Anatole]. Brenton English Zechariah 3:8: “Hear now, Jesus the high priest, thou, and thy neighbours that are sitting before thee: for they are diviners, for, behold, I bring forth my servant The Branch.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC03.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/3/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC03.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/ZEC03.htm.

reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
The Hebrew word names a shoot or sprout. The Greek word Ἀνατολή means a rising (of the sun or a star) and the East. Brenton’s English margin at this verse points to Luke 1:78. A reader can therefore set the KJV’s plant image beside the Greek’s rising image for the same servant.

Additional retained draft evidence/qualification:
The Hebrew word מוֹפֵת means a sign or wonder (the KJV margin has “of wonder, or, sign”). The Greek compound τερατοσκόποι is built from “portent” and “watch”, and Brenton’s English renders it “diviners”. A reader of the KJV has companions who are themselves a sign; a reader of the Greek has companions who watch portents.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew edition quoted has עַבְדִּי צֶמַח, “my servant Tsemach”, the word the KJV prints as BRANCH, from the sense of something that sprouts. The Greek printed has Ἀνατολήν, which is the ordinary Greek word for a rising and for the east. The KJV puts a growth image in the verse; the Greek puts a rising image. Both translators treat the word as a title or name.

title: The stone with seven eyes — “I will engrave the graving thereof” in the Hebrew, “I am digging a trench” in the Greek
summary: The KJV has the LORD engrave an engraving on the stone. The Hebrew is מְפַתֵּחַ פִּתֻּחָהּ. Brenton’s Greek is ὀρύσσω βόθρον, “I am digging a pit”, and goes on to say the LORD “will search out” the iniquity of the land.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Zechariah 3:9: “For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes: behold, I will engrave the graving thereof, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.” Hebrew (WLC) Zechariah 3:9: כִּ֣י ׀ הִנֵּ֣ה הָאֶ֗בֶן אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָתַ֙תִּי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹושֻׁ֔עַ עַל־אֶ֥בֶן אַחַ֖ת שִׁבְעָ֣ה עֵינָ֑יִם הִנְנִ֧י מְפַתֵּ֣חַ פִּתֻּחָ֗הּ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאֹ֔ות וּמַשְׁתִּ֛י אֶת־עֲוֹ֥ן הָאָֽרֶץ־הַהִ֖יא בְּיֹ֥ום אֶחָֽד׃ [behold I am engraving its engraving, utterance of the LORD of hosts]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Zechariah 3:9: Διότι ὁ λίθος ὃν ἔδωκα πρὸ προσώπου τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐπὶ τὸν λίθον τὸν ἕνα ἑπτὰ ὀφθαλμοί εἰσιν· ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ὀρύσσω βόθρον, λέγει Κύριος παντοκράτωρ, καὶ ψηλαφήσω πᾶσαν τὴν ἀδικίαν τῆς γῆς ἐκείνης ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ. [behold I am digging a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will probe all the iniquity of that land in one day]. Brenton English Zechariah 3:9: “For as for the stone which I have set before the face of Jesus, on the one stone are seven eyes: behold, I am digging a trench, saith the Lord Almighty, and I will search out all the iniquity of that land in one day.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC03.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/3/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC03.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/ZEC03.htm.

[“behold, I dig a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will search out all the injustice of that land in one day”] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC03.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/3/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC03.htm.
reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
In the Hebrew the LORD cuts an inscription on the stone that has seven eyes. In the Greek he digs a pit and then probes the land’s iniquity. The two images are different: carving a stone against digging the ground. The following clause also differs (“remove” against “search out”): the KJV has the LORD take the iniquity away, the Greek has him examine it.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew edition quoted has הִנְנִי מְפַתֵּחַ פִּתֻּחָהּ, “behold I am engraving its engraving”, and וּמַשְׁתִּי אֶת־עֲוֹן הָאָרֶץ, “I will remove (or remove the guilt of) the iniquity of the land”. The Greek printed has the verb ὀρύσσω with the noun βόθρον, “I dig a pit”, and ψηλαφήσω, “I will grope for, search out”. The KJV has the stone being engraved and the guilt taken away; the Greek has a pit dug and the unrighteousness searched out.

title: Cities going to worship — “one city to another” in the Hebrew, “five cities into one city” in the Greek
summary: The KJV has the inhabitants of one city go to another, saying let us go and pray. The Hebrew is יֹשְׁבֵי אַחַת אֶל־אַחַת, “inhabitants of one to one”. Brenton’s Greek has the inhabitants of five cities assemble into one city.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV Zechariah 8:21: “And the inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, Let us go speedily to pray before the Lord, and to seek the Lord of hosts: I will go also.” Hebrew (WLC) Zechariah 8:21: וְֽהָלְכ֡וּ יֹשְׁבֵי֩ אַחַ֨ת אֶל־אַחַ֜ת לֵאמֹ֗ר נֵלְכָ֤ה הָלֹוךְ֙ לְחַלֹּות֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וּלְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאֹ֑ות אֵלְכָ֖ה גַּם־אָֽנִי׃ [and the inhabitants of one will go to another, saying, Let us go to entreat the face of the LORD]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Zechariah 8:21: καὶ συνελεύσονται κατοικοῦντες πέντε πόλεις εἰς μίαν πόλιν, λέγοντες, πορευθῶμεν δεηθῆναι τοῦ προσώπου Κυρίου, καὶ ἐκζητῆσαι τὸ πρόσωπον Κυρίου παντοκράτορος· πορεύσομαι κᾀγώ· [and the inhabitants of five cities will come together into one city, saying, Let us go to beseech the face of the Lord]. Brenton English Zechariah 8:21: “and the inhabitants of five cities shall come together to one city, saying, Let us go to make supplication to the Lord, and to seek the face of the Lord Almighty; I will go also.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC08.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/8/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC08.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/ZEC08.htm.

title: The king’s rule — “he shall speak peace unto the heathen” in the Hebrew, “multitude and peace out of the nations” in the Greek
summary: The KJV says the king shall speak peace unto the heathen (nations). The Hebrew is וְדִבֶּר שָׁלוֹם לַגּוֹיִם. Brenton’s Greek is καὶ πλῆθος καὶ εἰρήνη ἐξ ἐθνῶν, “and multitude and peace from the nations”, and it describes the rule as over waters to the sea and the outlets of rivers of the land.
text:

title: “Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls” — Brenton’s Greek prints “shall be inhabited fruitfully”

title: “A bastard shall dwell in Ashdod” — Brenton’s Greek prints “strangers shall dwell in Azotus”

text: KJV Zechariah 9:6: “And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.” Hebrew (WLC) 9:6: וְיָשַׁ֥ב מַמְזֵ֖ר בְּאַשְׁדֹּ֑וד וְהִכְרַתִּ֖י גְּאֹ֥ון פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ Brenton’s Greek 9:6: Καὶ κατοικήσουσιν ἀλλογενεῖς ἐν Ἀζώτῳ, καὶ καθελῶ ὕβριν ἀλλοφύλων, [“And foreigners will dwell in Azotus, and I will bring down the pride of the Philistines”] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC09.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/9/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC09.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has וְיָשַׁב מַמְזֵר בְּאַשְׁדּוֹד, “and a mamzer shall dwell in Ashdod”, a singular noun. The Greek printed has the plural ἀλλογενεῖς, “people of another race”, and the Greek form Azotus for the city. The KJV puts a person of illegitimate birth there; the Greek puts foreigners there.
scope: T applies at Zechariah 9:6 only. title: “Shall go with whirlwinds of the south” — Brenton’s Greek prints “shall go in the shaking of his threatening”
summary: In the KJV of Zechariah 9:14 the Lord God shall go with whirlwinds of the south. Brenton’s Greek has πορεύσεται ἐν σάλῳ ἀπειλῆς αὐτοῦ, “he shall go in the tossing of his threat”, with no mention of the south.
text: KJV Zechariah 9:14: “And the Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning: and the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south.” Hebrew (WLC) 9:14: וַֽיהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יֵֽרָאֶ֔ה וְיָצָ֥א כַבָּרָ֖ק חִצֹּ֑ו וַֽאדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ בַּשֹּׁופָ֣ר יִתְקָ֔ע וְהָלַ֖ךְ בְּסַעֲרֹ֥ות תֵּימָֽן׃ Brenton’s Greek 9:14: καὶ Κύριος ἔσται ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς, καὶ ἐξελεύσεται ὡς ἀστραπὴ βολὶς, καὶ Κύριος παντοκράτωρ ἐν σάλπιγγι σαλπιεῖ, καὶ πορεύσεται ἐν σάλῳ ἀπειλῆς αὐτοῦ. [“and the Lord Almighty will sound the trumpet and will go in the tumult of his threatening”] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC09.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/9/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC09.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has וְהָלַךְ בְּסַעֲרוֹת תֵּימָן, “and he shall go in the storms of Teman”, where תֵּימָן means the south and is also a place name. The Greek printed has ἐν σάλῳ ἀπειλῆς αὐτοῦ, “in the tossing / tumult of his threat”, with no direction or place. The KJV gives a quarter of the compass for the storms; the Greek gives a threat.

title: “They shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign” — Brenton’s Greek prints “holy stones are rolled upon his land”
summary: In the KJV of Zechariah 9:16 the people shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon the Lord’s land. Brenton’s Greek has διότι λίθοι ἅγιοι κυλίονται ἐπὶ γῆς αὐτοῦ, “for holy stones are rolling on his land”.
text: KJV Zechariah 9:16: “And the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” Hebrew (WLC) 9:16: וְֽהֹושִׁיעָ֞ם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֛ם בַּיֹּ֥ום הַה֖וּא כְּצֹ֣אן עַמֹּ֑ו כִּ֚י אַבְנֵי־נֵ֔זֶר מִֽתְנֹוסְסֹ֖ות עַל־אַדְמָתֹֽו׃ Brenton’s Greek 9:16: Καὶ σώσει αὐτοὺς Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ, ὡς πρόβατα λαὸν αὐτοῦ, διότι λίθοι ἅγιοι κυλίονται ἐπὶ γῆς αὐτοῦ. [“and the Lord their God will save them in that day as the flock of his people, for holy stones roll upon his land”] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC09.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/9/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC09.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has כִּי אַבְנֵי־נֵזֶר מִתְנוֹסְסוֹת עַל־אַדְמָתוֹ, “for stones of a crown, being lifted high (as a banner), upon his ground”, with the participle מִתְנוֹסְסוֹת. The Greek printed has the adjective ἅγιοι, “holy”, for the crown, and the verb κυλίονται, “are rolled”. The KJV has crown stones raised up as an ensign; the Greek has holy stones rolling.
